articles.title: West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party members, says Union Minister as feuds rise in party
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: “BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP. The police administration has turned a blind eye and is not functioning impartially,” alleged Bongaon MP Santanu Thakur

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid reports of growing feuds within the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in West Bengal , Union Minister of State and Bongaon MP Shantanu Thakur not only publicly acknowledged factionalism within the party but also said that BJP supporters are attacked by its members. The Minister spoke about developments in his own constituency in North 24 Parganas, but reports of factional feuds within the BJP rank and file have surfaced across the State. “Here, BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP. The police administration has turned a blind eye and is not functioning impartially,” Mr. Thakur, who is the Bongaon MP and also a prominent leader of the Matua community, alleged. The Minister, who hails from Thakurbari and is the religious head of the Matua community, said that divisions are emerging within the party, resulting in major problems. Differences between Shantanu Thakur, the Bongaon North MLA, and State Food and Civil Supplies Minister Ashok Kirtania have been going around in political circles. On Sunday, BJP’s Panihati MLA Ratna Debnath, while expressing condolences over the death of a BJP worker, said that it would have been better “had the BJP not come to power in the State.” Arup Saha, husband of Ruma Saha—the secretary of BJP’s Panihati-1 Mandal (zone)—was attacked on Saturday (November 14, 2026), by a mob that allegedly included some of the party’s supporters. Saha succumbed to his injuries on Sunday. Reports of an intra-party feud have surfaced between long-time supporters of the ruling party in the State and former Trinamool Congress supporters who switched allegiance after the Assembly election results in May 2026. Political observers say that the majority of the BJP leadership, including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, had joined the party about five to six years ago.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has repeatedly said that the doors of the party are closed for Trinamool supporters who want to join. Mr. Bhattacharya said that an FIR should be registered against elements who are trying to associate with the party and tarnish its image. “Register FIRs. Suvendu Adhikari is the police minister. Give me the papers; I will file them,” Mr. Bhattacharya said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party members, says Union Minister as feuds rise in party

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 09:02:18 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: “BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP. The police administration has turned a blind eye and is not functioning impartially,” alleged Bongaon MP Santanu Thakur

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Amid reports of growing feuds within the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in West Bengal , Union Minister of State and Bongaon MP Shantanu Thakur not only publicly acknowledged factionalism within the party but also said that BJP supporters are attacked by its members. The Minister spoke about developments in his own constituency in North 24 Parganas, but reports of factional feuds within the BJP rank and file have surfaced across the State. “Here, BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP. The police administration has turned a blind eye and is not functioning impartially,” Mr. Thakur, who is the Bongaon MP and also a prominent leader of the Matua community, alleged. The Minister, who hails from Thakurbari and is the religious head of the Matua community, said that divisions are emerging within the party, resulting in major problems. Differences between Shantanu Thakur, the Bongaon North MLA, and State Food and Civil Supplies Minister Ashok Kirtania have been going around in political circles. On Sunday, BJP’s Panihati MLA Ratna Debnath, while expressing condolences over the death of a BJP worker, said that it would have been better “had the BJP not come to power in the State.” Arup Saha, husband of Ruma Saha—the secretary of BJP’s Panihati-1 Mandal (zone)—was attacked on Saturday (November 14, 2026), by a mob that allegedly included some of the party’s supporters. Saha succumbed to his injuries on Sunday. Reports of an intra-party feud have surfaced between long-time supporters of the ruling party in the State and former Trinamool Congress supporters who switched allegiance after the Assembly election results in May 2026. Political observers say that the majority of the BJP leadership, including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, had joined the party about five to six years ago.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has repeatedly said that the doors of the party are closed for Trinamool supporters who want to join. Mr. Bhattacharya said that an FIR should be registered against elements who are trying to associate with the party and tarnish its image. “Register FIRs. Suvendu Adhikari is the police minister. Give me the papers; I will file them,” Mr. Bhattacharya said.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Administration (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Allegiance (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Allegiance' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Factional (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Factional' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party members, says Union Minister as feuds rise in party", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. “BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own par' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own par' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "“BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP." (Hinglish Arth: “भाजपा कार्यकर्ताओं को पीटा जा रहा है, और उन्हें पीटने वाले भी भाजपा से हैं।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party members, says Union Minister as feuds rise in party"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Give me the papers; I will file them,” Mr.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Give me the papers; I will file them,” Mr." (Hinglish Arth: मुझे कागजात दो; मैं उन्हें दाखिल करूंगा,'' श्रीमान।)

articles.title: Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangalam traffic corridor in Keralam’s Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Developing the stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People’s representatives and officials on Monday conducted a site inspection for the proposed Goshree-Mamangalam road development project, which is expected to provide major relief from traffic woes in Kochi. The project is critical to improving the overall traffic system in the city and enhancing connectivity between various points. The demand for the proposed road dates back more than 30 years. Developing this stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads. A sum of ₹1 crore was earmarked for the development of Goshree Bridge and Goshree-Mamangalam Road in the last State Budget following interventions by Hibi Eden MP, MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, and Mayor V.K. Minimol. The allocation was intended for conducting a traffic study, demarcating the alignment, and completing the survey. An action plan will be formulated based on scientific studies and survey findings. Initially, the Goshree-Mamangalam road was proposed to be developed at 22 metres. However, during the tenure of the previous Kochi Corporation council, the width was scaled down to 15 metres in the 2024 Master Plan, which was subsequently approved by the State government. Based on this, follow-up measures are now being planned. Coordination among various departments is essential, as several roads within the Kochi Corporation limits form part of the project. Accordingly, the PWD (Roads) will be entrusted with conducting the traffic study, carrying out the survey and preparing a detailed project report. 🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangalam traffic corridor in Keralam’s Kochi

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 01:53:24 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Developing the stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: People’s representatives and officials on Monday conducted a site inspection for the proposed Goshree-Mamangalam road development project, which is expected to provide major relief from traffic woes in Kochi. The project is critical to improving the overall traffic system in the city and enhancing connectivity between various points. The demand for the proposed road dates back more than 30 years. Developing this stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease the existing pressure on several roads. A sum of ₹1 crore was earmarked for the development of Goshree Bridge and Goshree-Mamangalam Road in the last State Budget following interventions by Hibi Eden MP, MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, and Mayor V.K. Minimol. The allocation was intended for conducting a traffic study, demarcating the alignment, and completing the survey. An action plan will be formulated based on scientific studies and survey findings. Initially, the Goshree-Mamangalam road was proposed to be developed at 22 metres. However, during the tenure of the previous Kochi Corporation council, the width was scaled down to 15 metres in the 2024 Master Plan, which was subsequently approved by the State government. Based on this, follow-up measures are now being planned. Coordination among various departments is essential, as several roads within the Kochi Corporation limits form part of the project. Accordingly, the PWD (Roads) will be entrusted with conducting the traffic study, carrying out the survey and preparing a detailed project report. This is expected to facilitate the efficient and time-bound execution of the project through coordinated efforts by the Corporation and the PWD. The delegation assessed the existing condition of roads proposed to be included in the project, nature of traffic movement, development potential, and the role of the departments concerned. This is expected to aid the coordination of the proposed traffic study, survey, and subsequent follow-up measures.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: MLAs T.J. Vinod and Uma Thomas, Mayor V.K. Minimol, and deputy mayor V.R. Sudheer were among those who participated in the inspection.

समन्वय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Coordination' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

Development (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Corporation (Noun)

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangalam traffic corridor in Keralam’s Kochi", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Developing the stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangalam ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangal' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangal' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Developing the stretch into a major traffic corridor is expected to help resolve the city’s persistent traffic bottlenecks to a great extent and ease..." (Hinglish Arth: इस खंड को एक प्रमुख यातायात गलियारे के रूप में विकसित करने से शहर की लगातार यातायात बाधाओं को काफी हद तक हल करने और कई सड़कों पर मौजूदा दबाव को कम करने में मदद मिलने की उम्मीद है।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Site inspection held for key Goshree-Mamangalam traffic corridor in Keralam’s Kochi"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Sudheer were among those who participated in the inspection.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Sudheer were among those who participated in the inspection." (Hinglish Arth: निरीक्षण में भाग लेने वालों में सुधीर भी शामिल थे।)

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to bring light rainfall to parts of coastal T.N. on November 17
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The RMC, Chennai, has forecast that mainly dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State during this time

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: With the deep depression in the Bay of Bengal intensifying into cyclonic storm Akvan on Monday evening, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Chennai has issued a cyclone warning for Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts. The cyclonic storm lay centred about 610 km east of Chennai at 5.30 p.m. on Monday (November 16, 2026). The clouds associated with the system are likely to bring light to moderate rainfall at isolated places over coastal Tamil Nadu and the Western Ghat districts, as well as Puducherry and Karaikal, on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). The RMC, Chennai, has forecast that mainly dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State during the same period. Cyclone Akvan to make landfall between Nellore and Tuni in Andhra as very severe storm on November 20 Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra on November 20; Naidu reviews preparedness, 173 fishing boats yet to return Cyclone Akvan may bring rains to Telangana between November 19 and 21 For Wednesday (November 18, 2026) and Thursday (November 19, 2026), the RMC has forecast that heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places over Chennai, Tiruvallur, and Chengalpattu districts. The rain could be accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning, with gusty winds reaching speeds of 40-50 km/hour at one or two places. Heavy rain could occur at isolated places over Kancheepuram and Ranipet districts. Moderate rain is likely to occur at a few places over the rest of north coastal Tamil Nadu and the Western Ghat districts, Puducherry, and Karaikal. Light rain may occur in isolated places over the rest of Tamil Nadu, with thunderstorms and lightning at one or two places. A fisherman mends fishing net at Palavakkam beach in Chennai on November 16, 2026, as they remain ashore following an advisory against venturing into the sea from November 16 to 21 in view of impending Cyclone Akvan | Photo Credit: V. Umesh Kumar On Friday (November 20, 2026), moderate rain is likely in isolated places over the northern coastal districts of Tamil Nadu, the Western Ghat districts, Puducherry, and Karaikal. Light rain is likely at isolated places over the rest of Tamil Nadu, with thunderstorms and lightning at one or two places.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: It is very likely to continue moving north-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening. Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around Thursday morning.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Cyclone Akvan to bring light rainfall to parts of coastal T.N. on November 17

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 01:49:08 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The RMC, Chennai, has forecast that mainly dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State during this time

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: With the deep depression in the Bay of Bengal intensifying into cyclonic storm Akvan on Monday evening, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Chennai has issued a cyclone warning for Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts. The cyclonic storm lay centred about 610 km east of Chennai at 5.30 p.m. on Monday (November 16, 2026). The clouds associated with the system are likely to bring light to moderate rainfall at isolated places over coastal Tamil Nadu and the Western Ghat districts, as well as Puducherry and Karaikal, on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). The RMC, Chennai, has forecast that mainly dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State during the same period. Cyclone Akvan to make landfall between Nellore and Tuni in Andhra as very severe storm on November 20 Cyclone Akvan to hit Andhra on November 20; Naidu reviews preparedness, 173 fishing boats yet to return Cyclone Akvan may bring rains to Telangana between November 19 and 21 For Wednesday (November 18, 2026) and Thursday (November 19, 2026), the RMC has forecast that heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places over Chennai, Tiruvallur, and Chengalpattu districts. The rain could be accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning, with gusty winds reaching speeds of 40-50 km/hour at one or two places. Heavy rain could occur at isolated places over Kancheepuram and Ranipet districts. Moderate rain is likely to occur at a few places over the rest of north coastal Tamil Nadu and the Western Ghat districts, Puducherry, and Karaikal. Light rain may occur in isolated places over the rest of Tamil Nadu, with thunderstorms and lightning at one or two places. A fisherman mends fishing net at Palavakkam beach in Chennai on November 16, 2026, as they remain ashore following an advisory against venturing into the sea from November 16 to 21 in view of impending Cyclone Akvan | Photo Credit: V. Umesh Kumar On Friday (November 20, 2026), moderate rain is likely in isolated places over the northern coastal districts of Tamil Nadu, the Western Ghat districts, Puducherry, and Karaikal. Light rain is likely at isolated places over the rest of Tamil Nadu, with thunderstorms and lightning at one or two places.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: It is very likely to continue moving north-northwestwards and intensify further into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening. Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around Thursday morning.

मौसम विज्ञान और वायुमंडलीय परिवर्तनों से संबंधित (Connected with weather forecasting and atmospheric shifts).
✓ Syn: Atmospheric, Climatic, Weather-related  |  ✖ Ant: Geological, Subterranean, Terrestrial
Depression (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Depression' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Cyclonic (Adjective)
चक्रवाती — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Cyclonic' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Regional (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Regional' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Cyclone Akvan to bring light rainfall to parts of coastal T.N. on November 17", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The RMC, Chennai, has forecast that mainly dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State during this time.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Cyclone Akvan to bring light rainfall to parts o' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Cyclone Akvan to bring light rainfall to part' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Cyclone Akvan to bring light rainfall to part' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The RMC, Chennai, has forecast that mainly dry weather is likely to prevail over the rest of the State during this time." (Hinglish Arth: आरएमसी, चेन्नई ने पूर्वानुमान लगाया है कि इस दौरान राज्य के बाकी हिस्सों में मुख्य रूप से शुष्क मौसम रहने की संभावना है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Cyclone Akvan to bring light rainfall to parts of coastal T.N. on November 17"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around Thursday morning.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Thereafter, it is likely to move northwestwards and intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around Thursday morning." (Hinglish Arth: इसके बाद, इसके उत्तर-पश्चिम की ओर बढ़ने और गुरुवार सुबह के आसपास बहुत गंभीर चक्रवाती तूफान में तब्दील होने की संभावना है।)

articles.title: Kerala High Court refers petition challenging clean chit to Chief Minister in Punarjani case to Chief Justice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: High Court Registry directed to place the matter before the Chief Justice to decide whether the case would be considered by the court trying MP/MLA cases, Prevention of Corruption Act, or as a PIL

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Single Bench of the Kerala High Court has referred the petition challenging the closure of the preliminary inquiry against Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan in the Punarjani case for consideration before the appropriate court. Justice C. Jayachandran observed that there was a strong prima facie indication that the petition had features of a public interest litigation (PIL). The Bench directed the High Court Registry to place the matter before the Chief Justice to decide whether the case would be considered by the court trying MP/MLA cases, Prevention of Corruption Act, or as a PIL. The petition had been filed by lawyer K.M. Shajahan challenging a Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) report closing the preliminary inquiry and dropping corruption charges against the Chief Minister in connection with the Punarjani flood rehabilitation scheme. The court examined two aspects while considering the petition — first, if the petitioner had the right to challenge the preliminary inquiry report, and second, if the court had the jurisdiction to hear the matter. The petitioner argued that he had preferred the plea in his capacity as a citizen and a whistleblower, with every right to challenge the report. The State pointed out that a petition in this regard was filed by one of the complainants in the Punarjani case. This petition was later withdrawn and filed as a PIL seeking a CBI probe. However, the PIL was dismissed by a Division Bench of the court. The State contended that the petitioner did not have any right to move the petition since the complaint had already been decided by the court.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Single Bench found that the jurisdiction to try the case would have to be decided first before examining the rights of the petitioner.

However, the PIL was dismissed by a Division Bench of the court. The State contended that the petitioner did not have any right to move the petition since the complaint had already been decided by the court.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Single Bench found that the jurisdiction to try the case would have to be decided first before examining the rights of the petitioner.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: High Court Registry directed to place the matter before the Chief Justice to decide whether the case would be considered by the court trying MP/MLA cases, Prevention of Corruption Act, or as a PIL
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A Single Bench of the Kerala High Court has referred the petition challenging the closure of the preliminary inquiry against Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan in the Punarjani case for consideration before the appropriate court. Justice C. Jayachandran observed that there was a strong prima facie indication that the petition had features of a public interest litigation (PIL). The Bench directed the High Court Registry to place the matter before the Chief Justice to decide whether the case would be considered by the court trying MP/MLA cases, Prevention of Corruption Act, or as a PIL. The petition had been filed by lawyer K.M. Shajahan challenging a Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) report closing the preliminary inquiry and dropping corruption charges against the Chief Minister in connection with the Punarjani flood rehabilitation scheme. The court examined two aspects while considering the petition — first, if the petitioner had the right to challenge the preliminary inquiry report, and second, if the court had the jurisdiction to hear the matter. The petitioner argued that he had preferred the plea in his capacity as a citizen and a whistleblower, with every right to challenge the report. The State pointed out that a petition in this regard was filed by one of the complainants in the Punarjani case. This petition was later withdrawn and filed as a PIL seeking a CBI probe. However, the PIL was dismissed by a Division Bench of the court. The State contended that the petitioner did not have any right to move the petition since the complaint had already been decided by the court.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Single Bench found that the jurisdiction to try the case would have to be decided first before examining the rights of the petitioner.

articles.title: 70% turnout in most districts as four-phase panchayat polls end in Rajasthan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The declaration of results will bring the election of representatives in all 14,403 panchayats in the State to a close

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The four-phase panchayat election process in Rajasthan concluded on Monday with polling held for 3,747 sarpanch and 33,885 ward panch posts across 25 districts. Voting exceeded 70% in most of the districts that went to the polls in the final phase. There were stray incidents of confrontation and violence at some places, though long queues of voters were seen at several polling stations since morning. Villagers in Jalore district’s Gundau and Bharatpur district’s Shakarpur staged protests and created a ruckus raising allegations of bogus voting. Police fired in the air and used force to disperse the supporters of two rival candidates for the sarpanch post at Mahu Gulawali in Dholpur district. The two groups clashed and hurled stones at each other, while one of them set on fire two motorcycles parked outside a polling booth. In Dholpur’s Baroli village, polling started in late afternoon amid tension over a shooting incident on Sunday that resulted in the death of one person following a clash over election-related rivalry. Police have detained the main accused and 10 others in connection with the incident. The allegations of fraudulent voting sparked tension in Kali Pahadi village of Khairthal-Tijara district and a verbal altercation between two groups escalated into a physical confrontation. Police arrived in the village on receiving information and brought the situation under control. An elderly person, who sustained serious injuries during the clash, was referred to Alwar for treatment. Voting for both sarpanch and ward panch posts was conducted through ballot papers. More than 1.05 crore voters were eligible to exercise their franchise at 11,905 polling stations. Counting of votes started immediately after the polling ended. Results are expected to be declared by late night. The declaration of results will bring the election of representatives in all 14,403 panchayats in the State to a close.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The sarpanch and ward panch polls are not contested on political party symbols and parties do not officially allot tickets for these posts, unlike the zila parishad and panchayat samiti polls. Polling for zila parishad and panchayat samiti members across all four phases has been completed. Votes will be counted on November 20.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 70% turnout in most districts as four-phase panchayat polls end in Rajasthan

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 01:34:41 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The declaration of results will bring the election of representatives in all 14,403 panchayats in the State to a close

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The four-phase panchayat election process in Rajasthan concluded on Monday with polling held for 3,747 sarpanch and 33,885 ward panch posts across 25 districts. Voting exceeded 70% in most of the districts that went to the polls in the final phase. There were stray incidents of confrontation and violence at some places, though long queues of voters were seen at several polling stations since morning. Villagers in Jalore district’s Gundau and Bharatpur district’s Shakarpur staged protests and created a ruckus raising allegations of bogus voting. Police fired in the air and used force to disperse the supporters of two rival candidates for the sarpanch post at Mahu Gulawali in Dholpur district. The two groups clashed and hurled stones at each other, while one of them set on fire two motorcycles parked outside a polling booth. In Dholpur’s Baroli village, polling started in late afternoon amid tension over a shooting incident on Sunday that resulted in the death of one person following a clash over election-related rivalry. Police have detained the main accused and 10 others in connection with the incident. The allegations of fraudulent voting sparked tension in Kali Pahadi village of Khairthal-Tijara district and a verbal altercation between two groups escalated into a physical confrontation. Police arrived in the village on receiving information and brought the situation under control. An elderly person, who sustained serious injuries during the clash, was referred to Alwar for treatment. Voting for both sarpanch and ward panch posts was conducted through ballot papers. More than 1.05 crore voters were eligible to exercise their franchise at 11,905 polling stations. Counting of votes started immediately after the polling ended. Results are expected to be declared by late night. The declaration of results will bring the election of representatives in all 14,403 panchayats in the State to a close.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The sarpanch and ward panch polls are not contested on political party symbols and parties do not officially allot tickets for these posts, unlike the zila parishad and panchayat samiti polls. Polling for zila parishad and panchayat samiti members across all four phases has been completed. Votes will be counted on November 20.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Declaration (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Declaration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "70% turnout in most districts as four-phase panchayat polls end in Rajasthan", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The declaration of results will bring the election of representatives in all 14,403 panchayats in the State to a close.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of '70% turnout in most districts as four-phase panc' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to '70% turnout in most districts as four-phase p' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that '70% turnout in most districts as four-phase p' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The declaration of results will bring the election of representatives in all 14,403 panchayats in the State to a close." (Hinglish Arth: नतीजों की घोषणा के साथ राज्य की सभी 14,403 पंचायतों में प्रतिनिधियों का चुनाव संपन्न हो जाएगा)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "70% turnout in most districts as four-phase panchayat polls end in Rajasthan"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Votes will be counted on November 20.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Votes will be counted on November 20." (Hinglish Arth: वोटों की गिनती 20 नवंबर को होगी.)

articles.title: BJP holds key party meeting in Mathura for Assembly polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Senior BJP leaders from Uttar Pradesh, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attended a key meeting at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Cow Research Institute in Parkham, Mathura, to discuss strategy for the upcoming U.P. Assembly polls. The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach to counter the Opposition’s renewed pitch. “One goal, one idea... BJP government again for the third time... Today, in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, I participated in a planning meeting with National General Secretary (Organisation) B.L. Santosh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and BJP Uttar Pradesh Incharge Shri Vinod Tawde,” wrote Pankaj Chaudhary, U.P. BJP president, on X. “In the meeting, various important topics, including upcoming organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and providing benefits of public welfare schemes to every household, were discussed in detail. On this occasion, National General Secretary Irani, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya ji and Shri Brajesh Pathak, co-incharges of BJP Uttar Pradesh, Ministers of the State Government, public representatives, and state officials were present,” he added. State Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said the construction of a grand temple at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura will be a major poll issue in the 2027 U.P. elections, and that a grand Krishna temple will be built—through the courts or mutual dialogue, as with Ayodhya. “If Akhilesh Yadav wants to join us in kar seva, we will take him along too to build a grand temple of Lord Krishna,” said the Deputy CM. The meeting in Mathura is also significant amid the BJP’s emphasis on Mathura and western Uttar Pradesh. “The BJP holds meetings regularly to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment and other issues. Reach out to various sections of society is also part of our work,” said Dinesh Dubey, a senior BJP leader based in Lucknow. Asad Rizvi, a political analyst based in Lucknow, said, “the meeting is significant as it is organised only a few months before the Assembly elections. Amid the main Opposition parties (the Samajwadi Party-Congress) pushing backwards, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Brahmins and marginalised groups through the PDA plank, the BJP will be recalibrating their policies and making a renewed effort towards them. ”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SP president Akhilesh Yadav in a cryptic statement urged the BJP leaders to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. “I request them to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. It will be auspicious. If they fall ill, call a good doctor,” said Mr. Yadav.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 BJP holds key party meeting in Mathura for Assembly polls

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 04:57:22 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Senior BJP leaders from Uttar Pradesh, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attended a key meeting at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Cow Research Institute in Parkham, Mathura, to discuss strategy for the upcoming U.P. Assembly polls. The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach to counter the Opposition’s renewed pitch. “One goal, one idea... BJP government again for the third time... Today, in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, I participated in a planning meeting with National General Secretary (Organisation) B.L. Santosh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and BJP Uttar Pradesh Incharge Shri Vinod Tawde,” wrote Pankaj Chaudhary, U.P. BJP president, on X. “In the meeting, various important topics, including upcoming organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and providing benefits of public welfare schemes to every household, were discussed in detail. On this occasion, National General Secretary Irani, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya ji and Shri Brajesh Pathak, co-incharges of BJP Uttar Pradesh, Ministers of the State Government, public representatives, and state officials were present,” he added. State Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said the construction of a grand temple at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura will be a major poll issue in the 2027 U.P. elections, and that a grand Krishna temple will be built—through the courts or mutual dialogue, as with Ayodhya. “If Akhilesh Yadav wants to join us in kar seva, we will take him along too to build a grand temple of Lord Krishna,” said the Deputy CM. The meeting in Mathura is also significant amid the BJP’s emphasis on Mathura and western Uttar Pradesh. “The BJP holds meetings regularly to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment and other issues. Reach out to various sections of society is also part of our work,” said Dinesh Dubey, a senior BJP leader based in Lucknow. Asad Rizvi, a political analyst based in Lucknow, said, “the meeting is significant as it is organised only a few months before the Assembly elections. Amid the main Opposition parties (the Samajwadi Party-Congress) pushing backwards, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Brahmins and marginalised groups through the PDA plank, the BJP will be recalibrating their policies and making a renewed effort towards them. ”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SP president Akhilesh Yadav in a cryptic statement urged the BJP leaders to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. “I request them to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. It will be auspicious. If they fall ill, call a good doctor,” said Mr. Yadav.

संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Senior BJP leaders from Uttar Pradesh, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attended a key meeting at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Cow Research Institute in Parkham, Mathura, to discuss strategy for the upcoming U.P. Assembly polls. The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach to counter the Opposition’s renewed pitch. “One goal, one idea... BJP government again for the third time... Today, in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, I participated in a planning meeting with National General Secretary (Organisation) B.L. Santosh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and BJP Uttar Pradesh Incharge Shri Vinod Tawde,” wrote Pankaj Chaudhary, U.P. BJP president, on X. “In the meeting, various important topics, including upcoming organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and providing benefits of public welfare schemes to every household, were discussed in detail. On this occasion, National General Secretary Irani, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya ji and Shri Brajesh Pathak, co-incharges of BJP Uttar Pradesh, Ministers of the State Government, public representatives, and state officials were present,” he added. State Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said the construction of a grand temple at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura will be a major poll issue in the 2027 U.P. elections, and that a grand Krishna temple will be built—through the courts or mutual dialogue, as with Ayodhya. “If Akhilesh Yadav wants to join us in kar seva, we will take him along too to build a grand temple of Lord Krishna,” said the Deputy CM. The meeting in Mathura is also significant amid the BJP’s emphasis on Mathura and western Uttar Pradesh. “The BJP holds meetings regularly to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment and other issues. Reach out to various sections of society is also part of our work,” said Dinesh Dubey, a senior BJP leader based in Lucknow. Asad Rizvi, a political analyst based in Lucknow, said, “the meeting is significant as it is organised only a few months before the Assembly elections. Amid the main Opposition parties (the Samajwadi Party-Congress) pushing backwards, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Brahmins and marginalised groups through the PDA plank, the BJP will be recalibrating their policies and making a renewed effort towards them. ”
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SP president Akhilesh Yadav in a cryptic statement urged the BJP leaders to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. “I request them to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. It will be auspicious. If they fall ill, call a good doctor,” said Mr. Yadav.

articles.title: Tribute to Kartar Singh Sarabha, Punjab free from drugs and unemployment, says CM Mann
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the greatest tribute to the 19-year-old revolutionary and freedom fighter Kartar Singh Sarabha is to fulfil his dream of a Punjab free from drugs, unemployment, and injustice. He was speaking after paying tribute to Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha on his 111th martyrdom anniversary at his native village, Sarabha, in Ludhiana district. The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision. “Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha embraced the gallows at the tender age of just 19, proving that courage, conviction and love for the motherland know no age. At a time when youngsters today are planning their futures, this great revolutionary was planning the liberation of the country. He sacrificed his youth, dreams and ultimately his life for our freedom,” he said. “On November 16, 1915, Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged at Lahore Central Jail along with six other revolutionaries in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case. His fearless commitment to the freedom of the country remains a shining example of patriotism and selflessness,” he added. As the Punjab 2027 Assembly election approaches, the drug menace has once again become a central campaign issue. In the run-up to the Assembly polls, the major political parties in the fray—the Congress, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)—are making the drug menace a key plank of their campaigns.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While the ruling party has been asserting that eradicating drugs is its “biggest priority,” the Opposition parties have accused the AAP of failing to curb the drug menace and instead patronising the drug trade.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Tribute to Kartar Singh Sarabha, Punjab free from drugs and unemployment, says CM Mann

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 04:27:18 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the greatest tribute to the 19-year-old revolutionary and freedom fighter Kartar Singh Sarabha is to fulfil his dream of a Punjab free from drugs, unemployment, and injustice. He was speaking after paying tribute to Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha on his 111th martyrdom anniversary at his native village, Sarabha, in Ludhiana district. The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision. “Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha embraced the gallows at the tender age of just 19, proving that courage, conviction and love for the motherland know no age. At a time when youngsters today are planning their futures, this great revolutionary was planning the liberation of the country. He sacrificed his youth, dreams and ultimately his life for our freedom,” he said. “On November 16, 1915, Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged at Lahore Central Jail along with six other revolutionaries in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case. His fearless commitment to the freedom of the country remains a shining example of patriotism and selflessness,” he added. As the Punjab 2027 Assembly election approaches, the drug menace has once again become a central campaign issue. In the run-up to the Assembly polls, the major political parties in the fray—the Congress, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)—are making the drug menace a key plank of their campaigns.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While the ruling party has been asserting that eradicating drugs is its “biggest priority,” the Opposition parties have accused the AAP of failing to curb the drug menace and instead patronising the drug trade.

articles.title: Kishtwar killings aftermath: Remarks by Congress’ Karra, BJP’s Parihar spark protests in J&K
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Mr. Karra said that “two SPOs were killed by the Army in a mistaken-identity case on November 11”, while senior BJP leader Sharma said, “Congress is spreading misleading information to shift blame from terrorists to security forces”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two separate remarks made by J&K Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra and BJP legislator Shagun Parihar in the aftermath of the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar on Monday (November 16, 2026) sparked protests from different quarters. In response to the statement by Mr. Karra that “two SPOs were killed reportedly by the Army in a mistaken identity case on November 11”, senior BJP leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Sunil Sharma said, “The Congress is spreading misleading information to shift the blame from terrorists to our security forces. The SPOs were on duty and travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah to relieve the jawans posted there. Calling two martyrs hunters is an insult to their sacrifice and to their grieving families.” He demanded that Mr. Karra “immediately withdraw the remarks and apologise to the martyrs’ families, the J&K Police and the Indian Army”. Scores of members of the BJP and BJP-affiliated organisations held street protests against Mr. Karra and the Congress in Jammu. Members of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) also burn an effigy of Mr. Karra as a mark of protest. BJYM leader Arun Prabhat, while condemning the statement of Mr. Karra, said, “It shows the hearts of Congress beat for Pakistan. The conspirators should face action. In case of any role of mosques, such places too should face action.” Mr. Prabhat was seconding the controversial remarks of Ms. Parihar of the BJP, who claimed “announcements were made from the mosques in Kishtwar’s Dachhan area to identify the targets” allegedly ahead of the killings of two SPOs on November 11. However, several religious organisations, including the Anjuman Islamia Bhaderwah and Kishtwar, in the Chenab Valley condemned the statement of Ms. Parihar and denied any role of mosques in the latest attack on the policemen. Ruling National Conference (NC) legislator Tanvir Sadiq said the BJP must be “held accountable for its MLA’s deeply irresponsible and inflammatory allegations against a mosque in Jammu”. “Making communal allegations in the aftermath of a tragic killing is utterly unacceptable. The BJP leadership cannot hide behind silence or pretend this is an isolated matter. It must unequivocally condemn these remarks and issue an unconditional public apology. Stop playing with the communal harmony of J&K,” said Mr. Sadiq. A spokesman of the All J&K Shia Association said the organisation “strongly condemn Ms. Parihar’s attempt to drag a mosque into the tragic killing of our brave SPOs”. “Terrorists are enemies of all humanity and terrorism has no religion. Unsubstantiated claims against a place of worship only weaken our fight against terror,” said the Association.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Jammu and Kashmir / Indian National Congress / Bharatiya Janata Party

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Kishtwar killings aftermath: Remarks by Congress’ Karra, BJP’s Parihar spark protests in J&K

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 03:36:43 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Mr. Karra said that “two SPOs were killed by the Army in a mistaken-identity case on November 11”, while senior BJP leader Sharma said, “Congress is spreading misleading information to shift blame from terrorists to security forces”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two separate remarks made by J&K Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra and BJP legislator Shagun Parihar in the aftermath of the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar on Monday (November 16, 2026) sparked protests from different quarters. In response to the statement by Mr. Karra that “two SPOs were killed reportedly by the Army in a mistaken identity case on November 11”, senior BJP leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Sunil Sharma said, “The Congress is spreading misleading information to shift the blame from terrorists to our security forces. The SPOs were on duty and travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah to relieve the jawans posted there. Calling two martyrs hunters is an insult to their sacrifice and to their grieving families.” He demanded that Mr. Karra “immediately withdraw the remarks and apologise to the martyrs’ families, the J&K Police and the Indian Army”. Scores of members of the BJP and BJP-affiliated organisations held street protests against Mr. Karra and the Congress in Jammu. Members of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) also burn an effigy of Mr. Karra as a mark of protest. BJYM leader Arun Prabhat, while condemning the statement of Mr. Karra, said, “It shows the hearts of Congress beat for Pakistan. The conspirators should face action. In case of any role of mosques, such places too should face action.” Mr. Prabhat was seconding the controversial remarks of Ms. Parihar of the BJP, who claimed “announcements were made from the mosques in Kishtwar’s Dachhan area to identify the targets” allegedly ahead of the killings of two SPOs on November 11. However, several religious organisations, including the Anjuman Islamia Bhaderwah and Kishtwar, in the Chenab Valley condemned the statement of Ms. Parihar and denied any role of mosques in the latest attack on the policemen. Ruling National Conference (NC) legislator Tanvir Sadiq said the BJP must be “held accountable for its MLA’s deeply irresponsible and inflammatory allegations against a mosque in Jammu”. “Making communal allegations in the aftermath of a tragic killing is utterly unacceptable. The BJP leadership cannot hide behind silence or pretend this is an isolated matter. It must unequivocally condemn these remarks and issue an unconditional public apology. Stop playing with the communal harmony of J&K,” said Mr. Sadiq. A spokesman of the All J&K Shia Association said the organisation “strongly condemn Ms. Parihar’s attempt to drag a mosque into the tragic killing of our brave SPOs”. “Terrorists are enemies of all humanity and terrorism has no religion. Unsubstantiated claims against a place of worship only weaken our fight against terror,” said the Association.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Jammu and Kashmir / Indian National Congress / Bharatiya Janata Party

• 1. Core Context & Background: Mr. Karra said that “two SPOs were killed by the Army in a mistaken-identity case on November 11”, while senior BJP leader Sharma said, “Congress is spreading misleading information to shift blame from terrorists to security forces”
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two separate remarks made by J&K Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra and BJP legislator Shagun Parihar in the aftermath of the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar on Monday (November 16, 2026) sparked protests from different quarters. In response to the statement by Mr. Karra that “two SPOs were killed reportedly by the Army in a mistaken identity case on November 11”, senior BJP leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Sunil Sharma said, “The Congress is spreading misleading information to shift the blame from terrorists to our security forces. The SPOs were on duty and travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah to relieve the jawans posted there. Calling two martyrs hunters is an insult to their sacrifice and to their grieving families.” He demanded that Mr. Karra “immediately withdraw the remarks and apologise to the martyrs’ families, the J&K Police and the Indian Army”. Scores of members of the BJP and BJP-affiliated organisations held street protests against Mr. Karra and the Congress in Jammu. Members of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) also burn an effigy of Mr. Karra as a mark of protest. BJYM leader Arun Prabhat, while condemning the statement of Mr. Karra, said, “It shows the hearts of Congress beat for Pakistan. The conspirators should face action. In case of any role of mosques, such places too should face action.” Mr. Prabhat was seconding the controversial remarks of Ms. Parihar of the BJP, who claimed “announcements were made from the mosques in Kishtwar’s Dachhan area to identify the targets” allegedly ahead of the killings of two SPOs on November 11. However, several religious organisations, including the Anjuman Islamia Bhaderwah and Kishtwar, in the Chenab Valley condemned the statement of Ms. Parihar and denied any role of mosques in the latest attack on the policemen. Ruling National Conference (NC) legislator Tanvir Sadiq said the BJP must be “held accountable for its MLA’s deeply irresponsible and inflammatory allegations against a mosque in Jammu”. “Making communal allegations in the aftermath of a tragic killing is utterly unacceptable. The BJP leadership cannot hide behind silence or pretend this is an isolated matter. It must unequivocally condemn these remarks and issue an unconditional public apology. Stop playing with the communal harmony of J&K,” said Mr. Sadiq. A spokesman of the All J&K Shia Association said the organisation “strongly condemn Ms. Parihar’s attempt to drag a mosque into the tragic killing of our brave SPOs”. “Terrorists are enemies of all humanity and terrorism has no religion. Unsubstantiated claims against a place of worship only weaken our fight against terror,” said the Association.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Jammu and Kashmir / Indian National Congress / Bharatiya Janata Party

• 1. Core Context & Background: Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some of the U.S.’ largest banks on Monday (November 16, 2026). Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com. Chase Bank’s services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday (November 16, 2026). “Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.” The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began on Friday (November 13, 2026) and lasted for hours, which impacted services including Outlook, Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Some Chase customers received a message that said, “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan brews over Bay of Bengal: What you need to know
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Cyclone Akvan may intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal by Tuesday (November 17, 2026)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A weather system brewing over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm on Monday evening (November 16, 2026), according to the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD). It is moving north-northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh at 10 kmph and has been named ‘Akvan’, a name suggested by Iran under the North Indian Ocean naming list. CS Akvan over central adj westcentral BoB at 0530IST 17 Nov 610km E of Chennai 630km NE of Trincomalee 660km SE of Machilipatnam 670km SSE of Visakhapatnam 790km S of Gopalpur. Likely SCS today VSCS on 19th. Crossing AP coast as VSCS on 20th Nov. https://t.co/Qc2SeQNUPU It originated as a well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal on Saturday (November 14, 2026), the system intensified into a depression by Sunday (November 15, 2026) morning. The storm may continue to move north-northwestwards and intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal by Tuesday (November 17, 2026) evening and may cross the A.P. coast around noon on November 20, as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm, with windspeed gusting to 145 kmph, similar to that of Arnab. The system is forecast to bypass Tamil Nadu and move toward the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19, 2026, also impacting Odisha. ALSO WATCH Odisha braces for possible third cyclone in three weeks as Bay of Bengal system intensifies Heavy rainfall warnings have been issued for coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Andaman and Nicobar Islands through November 20, 2026. In West Bengal, heavy rain is forecast for South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur from November 19 to 21, 2026, with downpour likely in the southern districts of Howrah, Paschim Medinipur and Jhargram on November 20 and 21. According to the IMD, thunderstorms, accompanied with winds up to 40 kmph in Kolkata and most districts of Gangetic West Bengal is also likely. A nip in the air over South Bengal is likely to dissipate as day and night temperatures will rise by two to three degrees Celsius from November 18, 2026, it said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Cyclone Akvan is expected to cause rains in north coastal districts in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal area, it said.

📰 Cyclone Akvan brews over Bay of Bengal: What you need to know

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 10:50:55 AM

1. Core Context & Background: Cyclone Akvan may intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal by Tuesday (November 17, 2026)

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A weather system brewing over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm on Monday evening (November 16, 2026), according to the Indian Meteorological Department (IMD). It is moving north-northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh at 10 kmph and has been named ‘Akvan’, a name suggested by Iran under the North Indian Ocean naming list. CS Akvan over central adj westcentral BoB at 0530IST 17 Nov 610km E of Chennai 630km NE of Trincomalee 660km SE of Machilipatnam 670km SSE of Visakhapatnam 790km S of Gopalpur. Likely SCS today VSCS on 19th. Crossing AP coast as VSCS on 20th Nov. https://t.co/Qc2SeQNUPU It originated as a well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal on Saturday (November 14, 2026), the system intensified into a depression by Sunday (November 15, 2026) morning. The storm may continue to move north-northwestwards and intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal by Tuesday (November 17, 2026) evening and may cross the A.P. coast around noon on November 20, as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm, with windspeed gusting to 145 kmph, similar to that of Arnab. The system is forecast to bypass Tamil Nadu and move toward the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19, 2026, also impacting Odisha. ALSO WATCH Odisha braces for possible third cyclone in three weeks as Bay of Bengal system intensifies Heavy rainfall warnings have been issued for coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Andaman and Nicobar Islands through November 20, 2026. In West Bengal, heavy rain is forecast for South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur from November 19 to 21, 2026, with downpour likely in the southern districts of Howrah, Paschim Medinipur and Jhargram on November 20 and 21. According to the IMD, thunderstorms, accompanied with winds up to 40 kmph in Kolkata and most districts of Gangetic West Bengal is also likely. A nip in the air over South Bengal is likely to dissipate as day and night temperatures will rise by two to three degrees Celsius from November 18, 2026, it said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Cyclone Akvan is expected to cause rains in north coastal districts in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal area, it said.

articles.title: No proof from ECI to show SIR was a ‘unanimous’ decision, Rahul Gandhi to Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The ECI’s October 26 affidavit, in response to a petition filed by INDIA bloc leaders led by Mr. Gandhi, denied any differences of opinion between the CEC and the Election Commissioners over the SIR process

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi told the Supreme Court on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the Election Commission of India (ECI) failed to produce any proof to establish its claim that the special intensive revision (SIR) was a “unanimous” decision made by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar , and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. “No minutes of the meeting, file notings, recorded approvals, agenda, deliberations or other primary material evidencing the participation and approval of all three members have been produced with the ECI counter-affidavit of October 26,” Mr. Gandhi submitted in his rejoinder. Mr. Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders have also separately filed an application containing a set of “interrogatories” directed at the CEC, the two Election Commissioners, and other senior ECI officials involved in the SIR. The pointed questions inquire about the number and details of each SIR file, as well as the specific occasions between February 19, 2025, and October 26, 2026, on which the two Election Commissioners objected in writing or expressed dissent or reservation regarding any matter related to the SIR, ECINET, Form 6, or the filing of appeals. The case is scheduled for hearing on November 17 before a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. The reported friction between Mr. Kumar and the two Election Commissioners over the SIR and the CEC’s allegedly unilateral and authoritarian conduct, had triggered widespread protests across India demanding his removal from office. The ECI’s October 26 affidavit, in response to a petition filed by INDIA bloc leaders led by Mr. Gandhi, denied any differences of opinion between the CEC and the Election Commissioners over the SIR process. Mr. Gandhi said the court must not accept such “bare assertions” from the ECI. He questioned why the affidavit was filed by the ECI when Mr. Kumar, Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Joshi were separately made respondents. The Opposition leader, represented by senior advocate A.M. Singhvi and advocate Prasanna S., said the EC chose not to explain when and where exactly the decision to conduct a nationwide SIR was made. The ECI affidavit’s blank assertions contradict its own Right to Information (RTI) response that “the Commission has so far not taken any decision on initiating a special intensive revision (SIR) across the country in 2025”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Gandhi said the ECI’s claim of a “unanimous” Commission did not quite agree with the fact that Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Joshi took the unprecedented step of writing directly to the Cabinet Secretary, conveying their displeasure over the conduct of affairs within the poll body during the SIR exercise.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 No proof from ECI to show SIR was a ‘unanimous’ decision, Rahul Gandhi to Supreme Court

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 06:43:16 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The ECI’s October 26 affidavit, in response to a petition filed by INDIA bloc leaders led by Mr. Gandhi, denied any differences of opinion between the CEC and the Election Commissioners over the SIR process

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi told the Supreme Court on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the Election Commission of India (ECI) failed to produce any proof to establish its claim that the special intensive revision (SIR) was a “unanimous” decision made by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar , and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. “No minutes of the meeting, file notings, recorded approvals, agenda, deliberations or other primary material evidencing the participation and approval of all three members have been produced with the ECI counter-affidavit of October 26,” Mr. Gandhi submitted in his rejoinder. Mr. Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders have also separately filed an application containing a set of “interrogatories” directed at the CEC, the two Election Commissioners, and other senior ECI officials involved in the SIR. The pointed questions inquire about the number and details of each SIR file, as well as the specific occasions between February 19, 2025, and October 26, 2026, on which the two Election Commissioners objected in writing or expressed dissent or reservation regarding any matter related to the SIR, ECINET, Form 6, or the filing of appeals. The case is scheduled for hearing on November 17 before a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. The reported friction between Mr. Kumar and the two Election Commissioners over the SIR and the CEC’s allegedly unilateral and authoritarian conduct, had triggered widespread protests across India demanding his removal from office. The ECI’s October 26 affidavit, in response to a petition filed by INDIA bloc leaders led by Mr. Gandhi, denied any differences of opinion between the CEC and the Election Commissioners over the SIR process. Mr. Gandhi said the court must not accept such “bare assertions” from the ECI. He questioned why the affidavit was filed by the ECI when Mr. Kumar, Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Joshi were separately made respondents. The Opposition leader, represented by senior advocate A.M. Singhvi and advocate Prasanna S., said the EC chose not to explain when and where exactly the decision to conduct a nationwide SIR was made. The ECI affidavit’s blank assertions contradict its own Right to Information (RTI) response that “the Commission has so far not taken any decision on initiating a special intensive revision (SIR) across the country in 2025”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Mr. Gandhi said the ECI’s claim of a “unanimous” Commission did not quite agree with the fact that Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Joshi took the unprecedented step of writing directly to the Cabinet Secretary, conveying their displeasure over the conduct of affairs within the poll body during the SIR exercise.

B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'No proof from ECI to show SIR was a ‘unanimous’ ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'No proof from ECI to show SIR was a ‘unanimou' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'No proof from ECI to show SIR was a ‘unanimou' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.

articles.title: Six Liangmai Naga civilians laid to rest in Manipur 187 days after abduction, killing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: United Naga Council president N.G. Lorho said May 13, 2026, would remain the darkest day in Manipur’s history

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The bodies of six Liangmai Naga civilians were laid to rest in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district on Monday (November 16, 2026), 187 days after they were abducted and subsequently killed almost a month later. The family of the deceased and Naga organisations had refused to claim the bodies — kept at the mortuary of the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences in Imphal since June 10 — until their demands were met. One of the main demands of the Naga civil bodies was the abrogation of the 2008 Suspension of Operations agreements with 25 Kuki-Zomi armed groups. The UNC and the families agreed to accept the bodies after receiving assurances of justice at a tripartite meeting involving the Union government, the Manipur government and Naga organisations in Guwahati on September 26, and after the completion of a safer alternative road for the people of Konsakhul village. The families received the bodies on Monday and transported them to their home village of Konsakhul in the Kuki-dominated Kangpokpi district for the final rites. People from various communities gathered for the funeral. Speaking at the funeral, United Naga Council (UNC) president N.G. Lorho said May 13, 2026, would remain the darkest day in Manipur’s history. “On that day, six Naga men were killed, mutilated, and dismembered at Leilon Vaiphei village by KNF-P (Kuki National Front-Presidential), Kuki militants, and Leilon villagers. Their bodies were treated in a manner that brings shame to the State of Manipur and to India before the whole world,” he said. He also noted that the funeral underscored the unity of the Nagas and other indigenous communities of Manipur. “Our land is being invaded and ravaged. Our people are being killed, displaced, and terrorised. If this incursion is not stopped, the very existence, identity, and future of the indigenous people of Manipur will be at stake,” Mr. Lorho said. The UNC, Manipur’s apex Naga organisation, urged the Centre to immediately end the “policy of appeasement and protection of militant groups” carrying out attacks and killings, and to fulfill its constitutional and moral responsibility to protect the lives, land, and identity of indigenous people.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The killing of three Thadou church leaders in an ambush in Kangpokpi district on May 13 prompted a series of abductions. The Thadous are divided over their Kuki identity.
