🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 What are the eight Articles of impeachment filed against U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth?

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 05:35:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Representative Thomas Massie, backed by lawmakers including Ro Khanna, has introduced eight Articles of Impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in the House; here’s what you should know about them

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: There is a major shift happening in Capitol Hill following the U.S. midterm elections, as Representative Thomas Massie supported by lawmakers, including Representative Ro Khanna, introduced eight Articles of impeachment against U.S. Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth. The Articles cite violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution, alongside misconduct involving civilian casualties and operations in Yemen and Venezuela. Mr. Hegseth, a former Fox News weekend host and one of President Donald Trump’s handpicked appointees in his second term as U.S. President, took charge of the Department of War despite lacking administrative experience commensurate with the post. Despite controversies surrounding his tenure, Mr. Trump has maintained his support and repeatedly dismissed suggestions of dismissing him. Here is the complete breakdown of the eight Articles of impeachment introduced in the formal House resolution. Article 1 charges Mr. Hegseth with executing unlawful military orders by launching hostilities against Iran on February 28, 2026. The resolution states that the military strikes violated Section 2(c) of the 1973 War Powers Resolution because Congress had not declared war, provided statutory authorisation or faced any national emergency caused by an attack by the Islamic Republic of Iran against the U.S. Article II focuses on Mr. Hegseth’s refusal to comply with Congress’s directive to withdraw U.S. forces from Iran. After both the House and Senate passed House Concurrent Resolution 86 (the first successful passage of such a legislative vehicle by both chambers of Congress in the history of the United States of America) to end unauthorised hostilities in June 2026, Mr. Hegseth allegedly directed the Department of Defence to ignore the resolution and continue with military strikes. As per Section 5 (b) of the War Powers Resolution, authorised military action must terminate within 60 days (after a report is submitted or is required to be submitted to Congress). Article III alleges Mr. Hegseth continued conducting hostile military operations in Iran beyond the mandatory statutory deadlines of May 1 and June 1, 2026, without congressional extensions. This Article accuses Mr. Hegseth of “cultivating a warmaking culture” and a “course of conduct that effected the systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defence infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians and non-military objects during military operations”, among other allegations.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: It specifically highlights the February 28, 2026, cruise missile strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Iran, which killed and wounded over 200 civilians, mostly children.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Representative Thomas Massie, backed by lawmakers including Ro Khanna, has introduced eight Articles of Impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in the House; here’s what you should know about them
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: There is a major shift happening in Capitol Hill following the U.S. midterm elections, as Representative Thomas Massie supported by lawmakers, including Representative Ro Khanna, introduced eight Articles of impeachment against U.S. Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth. The Articles cite violations of the 1973 War Powers Resolution, alongside misconduct involving civilian casualties and operations in Yemen and Venezuela. Mr. Hegseth, a former Fox News weekend host and one of President Donald Trump’s handpicked appointees in his second term as U.S. President, took charge of the Department of War despite lacking administrative experience commensurate with the post. Despite controversies surrounding his tenure, Mr. Trump has maintained his support and repeatedly dismissed suggestions of dismissing him. Here is the complete breakdown of the eight Articles of impeachment introduced in the formal House resolution. Article 1 charges Mr. Hegseth with executing unlawful military orders by launching hostilities against Iran on February 28, 2026. The resolution states that the military strikes violated Section 2(c) of the 1973 War Powers Resolution because Congress had not declared war, provided statutory authorisation or faced any national emergency caused by an attack by the Islamic Republic of Iran against the U.S. Article II focuses on Mr. Hegseth’s refusal to comply with Congress’s directive to withdraw U.S. forces from Iran. After both the House and Senate passed House Concurrent Resolution 86 (the first successful passage of such a legislative vehicle by both chambers of Congress in the history of the United States of America) to end unauthorised hostilities in June 2026, Mr. Hegseth allegedly directed the Department of Defence to ignore the resolution and continue with military strikes. As per Section 5 (b) of the War Powers Resolution, authorised military action must terminate within 60 days (after a report is submitted or is required to be submitted to Congress). Article III alleges Mr. Hegseth continued conducting hostile military operations in Iran beyond the mandatory statutory deadlines of May 1 and June 1, 2026, without congressional extensions. This Article accuses Mr. Hegseth of “cultivating a warmaking culture” and a “course of conduct that effected the systemic deterioration and removal of Department of Defence infrastructure that Congress had mandated by law to limit collateral damage to civilians and non-military objects during military operations”, among other allegations.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: It specifically highlights the February 28, 2026, cruise missile strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Elementary School in Iran, which killed and wounded over 200 civilians, mostly children.

articles.title: Assam elephant rescue operation turns violent, eight people arrested
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The incident occurred when Forest personnel tried to guide a female elephant, separated from a herd, back to the jungle it came from

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Eight people were detained in central Assam’s Hojai district after they clashed with Forest Department personnel on Monday night (November 16, 2026) during an operation to guide a female elephant back to the jungle it came from. The Forest officials fired “sera bullets” (pellets) from a pump-action gun to divert the elephant away from a human settlement. Five people were injured in the firing, triggering the mob violence and leaving two personnel injured. Forest officials claimed three people sustained pellet injuries. The injured, including one of the two personnel, were admitted to a local hospital for treatment. Divisional Forest Officer Nayan Jyoti Rajbongshi said a herd of elephants from the hills of Karbi Anglong entered the Hawaipur Reserve Forest in Hojai on Monday morning. Barring the female elephant, estimated to be 40 years old, the herd returned to Karbi Anglong a few hours later. “We received information about the movement of the female elephant, possibly separated from the herd, along a road in a revenue area. We managed to push it into the Hawaipur Reserve Forest,” he said. However, the elephant emerged from the forest around dusk and headed toward a village. The Forest personnel fired the pellets to drive it away, but some villagers were injured in the process. “The police brought the situation under control and picked up eight people who clashed with our personnel. The police recorded the statement of our personnel,” Mr. Rajbongshi said. Wildlife officials said people often obstruct rescue operations by gathering around a wild animal that strays out of a forest.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to Assam government data tabled in the 126-member Assembly in July, as many as 1,147 people and 246 elephants were killed in human-elephant conflicts in the State since 2016.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Assam elephant rescue operation turns violent, eight people arrested

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 08:43:09 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The incident occurred when Forest personnel tried to guide a female elephant, separated from a herd, back to the jungle it came from

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Eight people were detained in central Assam’s Hojai district after they clashed with Forest Department personnel on Monday night (November 16, 2026) during an operation to guide a female elephant back to the jungle it came from. The Forest officials fired “sera bullets” (pellets) from a pump-action gun to divert the elephant away from a human settlement. Five people were injured in the firing, triggering the mob violence and leaving two personnel injured. Forest officials claimed three people sustained pellet injuries. The injured, including one of the two personnel, were admitted to a local hospital for treatment. Divisional Forest Officer Nayan Jyoti Rajbongshi said a herd of elephants from the hills of Karbi Anglong entered the Hawaipur Reserve Forest in Hojai on Monday morning. Barring the female elephant, estimated to be 40 years old, the herd returned to Karbi Anglong a few hours later. “We received information about the movement of the female elephant, possibly separated from the herd, along a road in a revenue area. We managed to push it into the Hawaipur Reserve Forest,” he said. However, the elephant emerged from the forest around dusk and headed toward a village. The Forest personnel fired the pellets to drive it away, but some villagers were injured in the process. “The police brought the situation under control and picked up eight people who clashed with our personnel. The police recorded the statement of our personnel,” Mr. Rajbongshi said. Wildlife officials said people often obstruct rescue operations by gathering around a wild animal that strays out of a forest.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to Assam government data tabled in the 126-member Assembly in July, as many as 1,147 people and 246 elephants were killed in human-elephant conflicts in the State since 2016.

A. The incident occurred when Forest personnel tried to guide a female elephant, separated from a herd, back to the jungle it came from.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Assam elephant rescue operation turns violent, e' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Assam elephant rescue operation turns violent' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Assam elephant rescue operation turns violent' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: Rights beyond the pad: making menstrual health services work in every school
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Supreme Court has recognised menstrual health as a constitutional right and laid down obligations for schools and governments. The real challenge now is making these services function reliably, every month, in every school

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court’s January 2026 judgment in Dr. Jaya Thakur v. Government of India recognised menstrual health as part of the right to life under Article 21 and directed States and Union Territories to provide free sanitary napkins, functional gender-segregated toilets, usable water and safe menstrual waste disposal facilities in every government and private school.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The success of this judgment, however, will not be measured in courtrooms. It will be measured in whether a girl can access a sanitary napkin, use a clean toilet with running water and dispose of menstrual waste safely.

articles.title: ‘Abki baar, AQI 400-paar’: Congress takes a swipe at Modi over Delhi pollution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Referring to reports of worsening air quality in Delhi, Jairam Ramesh said the city had become the most polluted in the world, with toxic air making breathing difficult

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Congress on Saturday (November 14, 2026) took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his 2024 Lok Sabha election slogan, “Abki baar, 400-paar”, saying it had come true in the national capital, with Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) crossing the 400-mark. In a post in Hindi on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said, “Abki baar, AQI 400-paar. The ‘pravachanmantri’s’ (preaching minister) slogan is coming true when it comes to AQI!” Referring to reports of worsening air quality in Delhi, Mr. Ramesh said the city had become the most polluted in the world, with toxic air making breathing difficult. Children and the elderly were bearing the brunt of the pollution, while the number of patients in hospitals was rising, he said. “Slogans were tossed into the air; now the air itself has turned to poison,” he said. Mr. Modi had used the “Abki baar, 400-paar” slogan during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, seeking a mandate of more than 400 seats for the National Democratic Alliance.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Several air quality monitoring stations in Delhi have recorded AQI levels in the ‘severe’ category (400-500) over the past few days. The city’s average AQI had also crossed the 400-mark on Friday (November 13, 2026).

articles.title: Three space companies selected to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction techniques for Indian cities
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, and the deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected three Indian space companies to develop High-Resolution Indian Human Settlement Layers (IHSL) across Indian cities. The three companies, SpacePixxel Technologies Pvt. Ltd. , KaleidEO Space Systems Pvt. Ltd. and Azista Industries Pvt. Ltd. have been selected under IN-SPACe’s Seed Fund Scheme for Use Case Demonstration by Non-Government Entities (NGEi) to develop IHSL across Indian cities. These companies will collectively receive seed funding of ₹1.46 crore to develop and demonstrate an indigenous satellite-based system for 3D reconstruction of India’s built environment using monocular imageries. IN-SPACe said that the initiative, undertaken under the Announcement of Opportunity (AO) for the development of high-resolution IHSL, aims to address the NITI Aayog’s requirement of having an accurate and detailed geospatial data on human settlement which can be used for urban planning, infrastructure development and disaster risk assessment in addition to population assessment. The selected companies will develop models using Earth Observation data to generate three integrated outputs covering built-up surface and building type, building height, and built-up volume. The deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying. The techniques will be developed at a high spatial resolution using Indian satellite data. The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, representing distinct urban contexts of a large metropolitan region and a hill city. The pilot project will derive settlement patterns across two time periods, enabling comparisons of urban growth and changes in built-up density over time. “India’s cities are expanding rapidly, both horizontally and vertically. Effective urban planning requires an accurate understanding of the built environment, but critical data gaps often limit this. This initiative addresses that gap by bringing together Indian satellite data, indigenous technology and clearly defined requirements from government departments. It gives Indian companies an opportunity to develop solutions for real-world urban challenges. More importantly, successful pilots can lay the foundation for scalable, homegrown capabilities that can be deployed across Indian cities,” Dr. Pawan Goenka, Chairman, IN-SPACe, said. “Starting with Bengaluru and Shimla, this IN-SPACe supported project will provide pathways to build indigenous satellite data on human settlements, allowing recognition of urbanisation as it happens.” said Shamika Ravi, Member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rajeev Jyoti, Director, Technical Directorate, IN-SPACe, said that the technical evaluation process was highly competitive, with 26 proposals received.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Three space companies selected to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction techniques for Indian cities

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 06:02:52 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, and the deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) has selected three Indian space companies to develop High-Resolution Indian Human Settlement Layers (IHSL) across Indian cities. The three companies, SpacePixxel Technologies Pvt. Ltd. , KaleidEO Space Systems Pvt. Ltd. and Azista Industries Pvt. Ltd. have been selected under IN-SPACe’s Seed Fund Scheme for Use Case Demonstration by Non-Government Entities (NGEi) to develop IHSL across Indian cities. These companies will collectively receive seed funding of ₹1.46 crore to develop and demonstrate an indigenous satellite-based system for 3D reconstruction of India’s built environment using monocular imageries. IN-SPACe said that the initiative, undertaken under the Announcement of Opportunity (AO) for the development of high-resolution IHSL, aims to address the NITI Aayog’s requirement of having an accurate and detailed geospatial data on human settlement which can be used for urban planning, infrastructure development and disaster risk assessment in addition to population assessment. The selected companies will develop models using Earth Observation data to generate three integrated outputs covering built-up surface and building type, building height, and built-up volume. The deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying. The techniques will be developed at a high spatial resolution using Indian satellite data. The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, representing distinct urban contexts of a large metropolitan region and a hill city. The pilot project will derive settlement patterns across two time periods, enabling comparisons of urban growth and changes in built-up density over time. “India’s cities are expanding rapidly, both horizontally and vertically. Effective urban planning requires an accurate understanding of the built environment, but critical data gaps often limit this. This initiative addresses that gap by bringing together Indian satellite data, indigenous technology and clearly defined requirements from government departments. It gives Indian companies an opportunity to develop solutions for real-world urban challenges. More importantly, successful pilots can lay the foundation for scalable, homegrown capabilities that can be deployed across Indian cities,” Dr. Pawan Goenka, Chairman, IN-SPACe, said. “Starting with Bengaluru and Shimla, this IN-SPACe supported project will provide pathways to build indigenous satellite data on human settlements, allowing recognition of urbanisation as it happens.” said Shamika Ravi, Member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Rajeev Jyoti, Director, Technical Directorate, IN-SPACe, said that the technical evaluation process was highly competitive, with 26 proposals received.

Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Indigenous (Adjective)
स्वदेशी — अपने ही देश (भारत) के वैज्ञानिकों और इंजीनियरों द्वारा देश में विकसित किया गया।
✓ Syn: Domestic, Home-grown, Native  |  ✖ Ant: Imported, Foreign, Exotic
Reconstruction (Noun)
पुनर्निर्माण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Reconstruction' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Comprehensive (Adjective)
विस्तृत — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Comprehensive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Three space companies selected to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction techniques for Indian cities", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, and the deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Three space companies selected to develop high-r' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Three space companies selected to develop hig' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Three space companies selected to develop hig' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, and the deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban..." (Hinglish Arth: पायलट प्रदर्शन बेंगलुरु और शिमला को कवर करेंगे, और डिलिवरेबल्स में शहरी बस्तियों के क्षैतिज और ऊर्ध्वाधर आयाम शामिल होंगे, जो कि भारतीय शहरों की अधिक व्यापक समझ प्रदान करेगा।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Three space companies selected to develop high-resolution 3D reconstruction techniques for Indian cities"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Rajeev Jyoti, Director, Technical Directorate, IN-SPACe, said that the technical evaluation process was highly competitive, with 26 proposals received.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Rajeev Jyoti, Director, Technical Directorate, IN-SPACe, said that the technical evaluation process was highly competitive, with 26 proposals received." (Hinglish Arth: IN-SPACe के तकनीकी निदेशालय के निदेशक, राजीव ज्योति ने कहा कि तकनीकी मूल्यांकन प्रक्रिया अत्यधिक प्रतिस्पर्धी थी, जिसमें 26 प्रस्ताव प्राप्त हुए थे।)

articles.title: Former Congress ally Gogoi tells Rahul Gandhi his parallel protests have weakened independent CJP mass movement
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Raijor Dal chief described the Cockroach Janata Party agitation as the most effective people’s movement against the BJP-RSS government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Raijor Dal president Akhil Gogoi, formerly an ally of the Congress in Assam, on Tuesday wrote to former Congress chief and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, urging him not to weaken the ongoing Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) movement by launching parallel protests and instead extend unconditional support to the “independent, youth-led people’s agitation”. Mr. Gogoi said the Congress had weakened the movement by competing with what he described was “a genuine mass revolt”, thereby dividing the Opposition’s street mobilisation. He also expressed concern over Mr. Gandhi’s silence on two earlier letters (dated October 29 and November 12, respectively), in which he sought clarity on the Congress’s approach to the movement and the Opposition’s strategy for the 2029 Lok Sabha election. “As someone who has spent his entire life on the streets fighting alongside peasants, workers, and the masses — not inside air-conditioned rooms — your continued silence troubles me deeply,” Mr. Gogoi wrote. He described the CJP agitation as the most effective people’s movement against the BJP-RSS government, claiming that it had mobilised the youth within five months in a manner that traditional Opposition politics had failed to achieve over the past 12 years. “You cannot defeat a fascist regime through party control or press conference politics. Real political change only happens through an honest, independent people’s movement backed unconditionally by the Opposition,” he said. Mr. Gogoi asked Mr. Gandhi to explain why the Congress had undermined the movement and what its position was on supporting an independent mass struggle. If the Congress had reservations about the CJP or its leadership, it should ensure that another strong mass movement, backed by the entire Opposition, was built to challenge the government, he said. “Let me state this clearly from decades of grassroots struggle: if there is no independent people’s movement, there is no chance of changing this communal, fascist government,” the Raijor Dal chief claimed.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a separate letter to political activist Yogendra Yadav, Mr. Gogoi accused Mr. Yadav and other activists, including Neha Bora and Left leaders, of allowing themselves to be used by the Congress to undermine the agitation.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Former Congress ally Gogoi tells Rahul Gandhi his parallel protests have weakened independent CJP mass movement

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 09:26:21 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Raijor Dal chief described the Cockroach Janata Party agitation as the most effective people’s movement against the BJP-RSS government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Raijor Dal president Akhil Gogoi, formerly an ally of the Congress in Assam, on Tuesday wrote to former Congress chief and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, urging him not to weaken the ongoing Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) movement by launching parallel protests and instead extend unconditional support to the “independent, youth-led people’s agitation”. Mr. Gogoi said the Congress had weakened the movement by competing with what he described was “a genuine mass revolt”, thereby dividing the Opposition’s street mobilisation. He also expressed concern over Mr. Gandhi’s silence on two earlier letters (dated October 29 and November 12, respectively), in which he sought clarity on the Congress’s approach to the movement and the Opposition’s strategy for the 2029 Lok Sabha election. “As someone who has spent his entire life on the streets fighting alongside peasants, workers, and the masses — not inside air-conditioned rooms — your continued silence troubles me deeply,” Mr. Gogoi wrote. He described the CJP agitation as the most effective people’s movement against the BJP-RSS government, claiming that it had mobilised the youth within five months in a manner that traditional Opposition politics had failed to achieve over the past 12 years. “You cannot defeat a fascist regime through party control or press conference politics. Real political change only happens through an honest, independent people’s movement backed unconditionally by the Opposition,” he said. Mr. Gogoi asked Mr. Gandhi to explain why the Congress had undermined the movement and what its position was on supporting an independent mass struggle. If the Congress had reservations about the CJP or its leadership, it should ensure that another strong mass movement, backed by the entire Opposition, was built to challenge the government, he said. “Let me state this clearly from decades of grassroots struggle: if there is no independent people’s movement, there is no chance of changing this communal, fascist government,” the Raijor Dal chief claimed.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a separate letter to political activist Yogendra Yadav, Mr. Gogoi accused Mr. Yadav and other activists, including Neha Bora and Left leaders, of allowing themselves to be used by the Congress to undermine the agitation.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Raijor Dal chief described the Cockroach Janata Party agitation as the most effective people’s movement against the BJP-RSS government
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Raijor Dal president Akhil Gogoi, formerly an ally of the Congress in Assam, on Tuesday wrote to former Congress chief and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, urging him not to weaken the ongoing Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) movement by launching parallel protests and instead extend unconditional support to the “independent, youth-led people’s agitation”. Mr. Gogoi said the Congress had weakened the movement by competing with what he described was “a genuine mass revolt”, thereby dividing the Opposition’s street mobilisation. He also expressed concern over Mr. Gandhi’s silence on two earlier letters (dated October 29 and November 12, respectively), in which he sought clarity on the Congress’s approach to the movement and the Opposition’s strategy for the 2029 Lok Sabha election. “As someone who has spent his entire life on the streets fighting alongside peasants, workers, and the masses — not inside air-conditioned rooms — your continued silence troubles me deeply,” Mr. Gogoi wrote. He described the CJP agitation as the most effective people’s movement against the BJP-RSS government, claiming that it had mobilised the youth within five months in a manner that traditional Opposition politics had failed to achieve over the past 12 years. “You cannot defeat a fascist regime through party control or press conference politics. Real political change only happens through an honest, independent people’s movement backed unconditionally by the Opposition,” he said. Mr. Gogoi asked Mr. Gandhi to explain why the Congress had undermined the movement and what its position was on supporting an independent mass struggle. If the Congress had reservations about the CJP or its leadership, it should ensure that another strong mass movement, backed by the entire Opposition, was built to challenge the government, he said. “Let me state this clearly from decades of grassroots struggle: if there is no independent people’s movement, there is no chance of changing this communal, fascist government,” the Raijor Dal chief claimed.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In a separate letter to political activist Yogendra Yadav, Mr. Gogoi accused Mr. Yadav and other activists, including Neha Bora and Left leaders, of allowing themselves to be used by the Congress to undermine the agitation.

articles.title: SC upholds stay on Azam Khan’s conviction in fake birth certificate case, extends relief to wife, son
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that denying the stay of conviction to Dr. Tazeen Fatma and Abdullah Azam Khan violated the doctrine of parity, but cautioned that the power to stay a conviction cannot be invoked for political expediency or electoral ambitions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) upheld the Allahabad High Court’s decision to stay the conviction of Samajwadi Party leader Mohammed Azam Khan in a case involving allegedly forged birth certificates obtained for his son, Abdullah Azam Khan. The court also stayed the convictions of Mr. Khan’s wife, Dr. Tazeen Fatma, and son in the same case. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu dismissed appeals filed by the Uttar Pradesh government against the High Court’s May 24, 2024, decision, while allowing separate appeals filed by Mr. Khan’s wife and son. “Though differential treatment is not forbidden, an unreasoned differential treatment cannot be sustained,” the Bench observed, holding that the High Court had failed to justify why Mr. Khan’s wife and son were denied the same relief despite being convicted on identical charges arising from the same alleged conspiracy. The Bench held that the High Court’s refusal to extend the stay of conviction to Mr. Khan’s wife and son violated the doctrine of parity and amounted to a jurisdictional error. It noted that the prosecution case against all three rested on the same allegation of criminal conspiracy involving the two conflicting birth certificates issued in Rampur and Lucknow. “Where the evidentiary foundation, the statutory offences, and the conspiracy matrix bind all three of the family to an identical legal fate, affording favourable treatment to the patriarch while denying a stay of conviction to his son and wife [who also happens to be a septuagenarian] constitutes an arbitrary differentiation. Both face the same irremediable prejudice, severe moral opprobrium, and irreversible loss of constitutional dignity during the pendency of their revision petitions,” the Bench said. The court also found no reason to interfere with the relief granted to Mr. Khan, noting that the High Court had considered his prolonged custody, advanced age and the absence of direct evidence that he had personally forged signatures in municipal records. The ruling, authored by Justice Datta, also observed that a conviction could cause irreparable harm to an individual’s reputation and dignity, which are integral to the right to life guaranteed under Article 21, even if subsequently overturned. The court held that the power to stay a conviction must therefore be exercised cautiously, balancing its potentially irreversible consequences against the sanctity attached to a conviction until it is set aside on appeal. The Bench, however, cautioned that the power could not be invoked merely to further political interests. “We unequivocally disavow and reject any plea that seeks a stay of conviction anchored purely on political expediency, electoral ambitions, or the exigencies of upcoming election campaigns. Courts of law cannot permit statutory powers to be leveraged to suit political calendars or electoral ambitions,” the Bench said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Accordingly, the Bench directed that the convictions of Mr. Khan’s wife and son remain stayed pending disposal of their criminal revision petitions before the High Court. It asked the High Court to decide the petitions expeditiously, uninfluenced by any observations made in its judgment.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 SC upholds stay on Azam Khan’s conviction in fake birth certificate case, extends relief to wife, son

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 09:26:17 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that denying the stay of conviction to Dr. Tazeen Fatma and Abdullah Azam Khan violated the doctrine of parity, but cautioned that the power to stay a conviction cannot be invoked for political expediency or electoral ambitions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) upheld the Allahabad High Court’s decision to stay the conviction of Samajwadi Party leader Mohammed Azam Khan in a case involving allegedly forged birth certificates obtained for his son, Abdullah Azam Khan. The court also stayed the convictions of Mr. Khan’s wife, Dr. Tazeen Fatma, and son in the same case. A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu dismissed appeals filed by the Uttar Pradesh government against the High Court’s May 24, 2024, decision, while allowing separate appeals filed by Mr. Khan’s wife and son. “Though differential treatment is not forbidden, an unreasoned differential treatment cannot be sustained,” the Bench observed, holding that the High Court had failed to justify why Mr. Khan’s wife and son were denied the same relief despite being convicted on identical charges arising from the same alleged conspiracy. The Bench held that the High Court’s refusal to extend the stay of conviction to Mr. Khan’s wife and son violated the doctrine of parity and amounted to a jurisdictional error. It noted that the prosecution case against all three rested on the same allegation of criminal conspiracy involving the two conflicting birth certificates issued in Rampur and Lucknow. “Where the evidentiary foundation, the statutory offences, and the conspiracy matrix bind all three of the family to an identical legal fate, affording favourable treatment to the patriarch while denying a stay of conviction to his son and wife [who also happens to be a septuagenarian] constitutes an arbitrary differentiation. Both face the same irremediable prejudice, severe moral opprobrium, and irreversible loss of constitutional dignity during the pendency of their revision petitions,” the Bench said. The court also found no reason to interfere with the relief granted to Mr. Khan, noting that the High Court had considered his prolonged custody, advanced age and the absence of direct evidence that he had personally forged signatures in municipal records. The ruling, authored by Justice Datta, also observed that a conviction could cause irreparable harm to an individual’s reputation and dignity, which are integral to the right to life guaranteed under Article 21, even if subsequently overturned. The court held that the power to stay a conviction must therefore be exercised cautiously, balancing its potentially irreversible consequences against the sanctity attached to a conviction until it is set aside on appeal. The Bench, however, cautioned that the power could not be invoked merely to further political interests. “We unequivocally disavow and reject any plea that seeks a stay of conviction anchored purely on political expediency, electoral ambitions, or the exigencies of upcoming election campaigns. Courts of law cannot permit statutory powers to be leveraged to suit political calendars or electoral ambitions,” the Bench said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Accordingly, the Bench directed that the convictions of Mr. Khan’s wife and son remain stayed pending disposal of their criminal revision petitions before the High Court. It asked the High Court to decide the petitions expeditiously, uninfluenced by any observations made in its judgment.

अधिकार क्षेत्र — न्यायालय या किसी संस्था की वह कानूनी सीमा जहाँ तक वह आदेश दे सके।
✓ Syn: Authority, Sovereignty, Cognizance  |  ✖ Ant: Powerlessness, Subordination, Incompetence

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Differentiation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

articles.title: Rajnath Singh to visit Japan for Ministerial dialogue on defence cooperation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The dialogue is expected to review the entire spectrum of bilateral strategic and defence cooperation, besides providing an opportunity to exchange views on regional and global developments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Japan on November 18 and 19 to participate in the fourth edition of the India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Dialogue (2+2) and hold bilateral discussions with his Japanese counterpart, with a focus on strengthening defence cooperation, maritime security and defence industrial partnerships. According to the Ministry of Defence, the 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue, scheduled to be held in Tokyo, will be co-chaired by Mr. Singh and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, along with Japan’s Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi. The dialogue is expected to review the entire spectrum of bilateral strategic and defence cooperation, besides providing an opportunity to exchange views on regional and global developments. The two sides will also reaffirm their commitment to a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, it added. The bilateral meeting between Mr. sSingh and Mr. Koizumi will be their third this year. The two Ministers had earlier met in New Delhi in August and on the sidelines of the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus in Cebu in October. During the upcoming discussions, the two sides are expected to deliberate on expanding defence equipment and technology collaboration, strengthening maritime security, enhancing the scale and complexity of joint military exercises across all three services and deepening defence industrial partnerships. India and Japan share a Special Strategic and Global Partnership founded on shared democratic values, mutual trust and converging strategic interests. The visit is aimed at further strengthening bilateral defence ties and identifying new avenues for operational cooperation and industrial collaboration.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The two countries have been steadily expanding their defence and security engagement, with greater emphasis on interoperability, technology cooperation and their shared strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Rajnath Singh to visit Japan for Ministerial dialogue on defence cooperation

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 09:25:35 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The dialogue is expected to review the entire spectrum of bilateral strategic and defence cooperation, besides providing an opportunity to exchange views on regional and global developments

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Japan on November 18 and 19 to participate in the fourth edition of the India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Dialogue (2+2) and hold bilateral discussions with his Japanese counterpart, with a focus on strengthening defence cooperation, maritime security and defence industrial partnerships. According to the Ministry of Defence, the 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue, scheduled to be held in Tokyo, will be co-chaired by Mr. Singh and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, along with Japan’s Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi. The dialogue is expected to review the entire spectrum of bilateral strategic and defence cooperation, besides providing an opportunity to exchange views on regional and global developments. The two sides will also reaffirm their commitment to a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, it added. The bilateral meeting between Mr. sSingh and Mr. Koizumi will be their third this year. The two Ministers had earlier met in New Delhi in August and on the sidelines of the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus in Cebu in October. During the upcoming discussions, the two sides are expected to deliberate on expanding defence equipment and technology collaboration, strengthening maritime security, enhancing the scale and complexity of joint military exercises across all three services and deepening defence industrial partnerships. India and Japan share a Special Strategic and Global Partnership founded on shared democratic values, mutual trust and converging strategic interests. The visit is aimed at further strengthening bilateral defence ties and identifying new avenues for operational cooperation and industrial collaboration.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The two countries have been steadily expanding their defence and security engagement, with greater emphasis on interoperability, technology cooperation and their shared strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region.

articles.title: Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists in 13 States and UTs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: These States/UTs saw their combined electorate shrink from 49.6 cr to 45.2 cr post-SIR, but SSR has resulted in a recovery to almost 46 cr in draft SSR list; U.P. has highest number of voters added through SSR, but Goa sees highest growth in percentage terms

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Months after final voters lists were published following the contentious special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, nearly 75 lakh more names have been added in draft voter lists published in 13 States and Union Territories via a special summary revision process (SSR). The combined size of the electorate in these States before the SIR was 49.61 crore, which shrunk to 45.22 crore after the SIR and has now increased to 45.96 crore in the draft SSR list. This means there has been a cumulative increase of 1.64 %. Uttar Pradesh, which published its draft SSR list on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), saw 18.84 lakh names being added to its voter lists, the largest in absolute numbers so far. Goa saw the highest rate of additions, at 3.01 %. Bihar, which was the first State to undergo the SIR process in 2025 saw 13.89 lakh names being added to the final post-SIR list. Rajasthan saw more than 11.48 lakh voters being added to the final SIR voter list, followed by Uttarakhand (1.19 lakh), Madhya Pradesh (8.9 lakh), and Tamil Nadu (10.39 lakh). The SSR, on hold since the SIR process began last year, was first announced in 17 States and UTs, including poll-bound Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab, on October 15. On November 5, it was expanded to six more States where the SIR process is over, and on November 16, it was announced that the SSR would also be conducted in Karnataka and Meghalaya. Of these, the draft SSR rolls have been published for 15 States and UTs. The data for Punjab and Gujarat, however, was not available. The SSR, an annual exercise, usually seeks to enrol eligible voters, particularly young and first-time electors, and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1, and October 1, 2027. However, it had not been carried out after the SIR was launched last year, an anomaly that was recently highlighted by Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. Unlike the now contentious SIR process, when enrolling through the SSR, voters do not need to provide any documentation proving citizenship or be mapped with earlier electoral rolls. Among the firsts, in this year’s SSR, the ECI has directed that, at the time of the polls, a “readable PDF” of the alphabetically arranged electoral rolls can be provided to the contesting candidates in a pen drive or any other electronic storage device. This is crucial as Opposition parties have been demanding machine-readable electoral rolls rather than image-based PDFs, so that they are digitally searchable, indexable, and verifiable. Political parties will also be provided with supplementary voter lists which were earlier kept only for records and future use.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SSR process this time not only features the usual house-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers, but also includes the publication and display of draft as well as final voter lists at the polling booths.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists in 13 States and UTs

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 09:25:09 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: These States/UTs saw their combined electorate shrink from 49.6 cr to 45.2 cr post-SIR, but SSR has resulted in a recovery to almost 46 cr in draft SSR list; U.P. has highest number of voters added through SSR, but Goa sees highest growth in percentage terms

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Months after final voters lists were published following the contentious special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, nearly 75 lakh more names have been added in draft voter lists published in 13 States and Union Territories via a special summary revision process (SSR). The combined size of the electorate in these States before the SIR was 49.61 crore, which shrunk to 45.22 crore after the SIR and has now increased to 45.96 crore in the draft SSR list. This means there has been a cumulative increase of 1.64 %. Uttar Pradesh, which published its draft SSR list on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), saw 18.84 lakh names being added to its voter lists, the largest in absolute numbers so far. Goa saw the highest rate of additions, at 3.01 %. Bihar, which was the first State to undergo the SIR process in 2025 saw 13.89 lakh names being added to the final post-SIR list. Rajasthan saw more than 11.48 lakh voters being added to the final SIR voter list, followed by Uttarakhand (1.19 lakh), Madhya Pradesh (8.9 lakh), and Tamil Nadu (10.39 lakh). The SSR, on hold since the SIR process began last year, was first announced in 17 States and UTs, including poll-bound Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab, on October 15. On November 5, it was expanded to six more States where the SIR process is over, and on November 16, it was announced that the SSR would also be conducted in Karnataka and Meghalaya. Of these, the draft SSR rolls have been published for 15 States and UTs. The data for Punjab and Gujarat, however, was not available. The SSR, an annual exercise, usually seeks to enrol eligible voters, particularly young and first-time electors, and facilitate advance applications from those who will become eligible on April 1, July 1, and October 1, 2027. However, it had not been carried out after the SIR was launched last year, an anomaly that was recently highlighted by Election Commissioners S.S. Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. Unlike the now contentious SIR process, when enrolling through the SSR, voters do not need to provide any documentation proving citizenship or be mapped with earlier electoral rolls. Among the firsts, in this year’s SSR, the ECI has directed that, at the time of the polls, a “readable PDF” of the alphabetically arranged electoral rolls can be provided to the contesting candidates in a pen drive or any other electronic storage device. This is crucial as Opposition parties have been demanding machine-readable electoral rolls rather than image-based PDFs, so that they are digitally searchable, indexable, and verifiable. Political parties will also be provided with supplementary voter lists which were earlier kept only for records and future use.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SSR process this time not only features the usual house-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers, but also includes the publication and display of draft as well as final voter lists at the polling booths.

Documentation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Documentation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Contentious (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Contentious' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Publication (Noun)
प्रकाशन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Publication' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Cumulative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cumulative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists in 13 States and UTs", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. These States/UTs saw their combined electorate shrink from 49.6 cr to 45.2 cr post-SIR, but SSR has resulted in a recovery to almost 46 cr in draft...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters l' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voter' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voter' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "These States/UTs saw their combined electorate shrink from 49.6 cr to 45.2 cr post-SIR, but SSR has resulted in a recovery to almost 46 cr in draft..." (Hinglish Arth: एसआईआर के बाद इन राज्यों/केंद्रशासित प्रदेशों का संयुक्त मतदाता वर्ग 49.6 करोड़ से घटकर 45.2 करोड़ हो गया, लेकिन एसएसआर के परिणामस्वरूप ड्राफ्ट एसएसआर सूची में लगभग 46 करोड़ की रिकवरी हुई है; ऊपर।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists in 13 States and UTs"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The SSR process this time not only features the usual house-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers, but also includes the publication and display of...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The SSR process this time not only features the usual house-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers, but also includes the publication and display of..." (Hinglish Arth: इस बार एसएसआर प्रक्रिया में न केवल बूथ स्तर के अधिकारियों द्वारा सामान्य घर-घर का दौरा शामिल है, बल्कि मतदान केंद्रों पर ड्राफ्ट के साथ-साथ अंतिम मतदाता सूचियों का प्रकाशन और प्रदर्शन भी शामिल है।)

articles.title: P.B. Siddhartha College to host international seminar on Viksit Bharat from November 19
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Parvathaneni Brahmayya Siddhartha College of Arts and Science, Vijayawada, will host a three-day international seminar on “Viksit Bharat @2047” from November 19 in collaboration with the Indian Economics and Allied Sciences Association (IEASA).

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: At a press conference on Tuesday, college Principal Meka Ramesh, Director Vemuri Babu Rao, Dean and conference convener Rajesh C. Jampala, and IEASA Secretary Alok Kumar released the brochure for the event, titled “7th Annual International Conference of IEASA: Viksit Bharat @2047 – Economic Resilience, Innovation and Sustainable Development in a Dynamic Global Landscape”. The inaugural session will be held at PVP Siddhartha College of Information Technology, while the subsequent sessions over the three days will be conducted at P.B. Siddhartha College of Arts and Science. Adani Group CEO (Skills and Education) Robin Bhowmik, Canara Bank General Manager and Circle Head Devaraj R. and Symboyzia Group Director G.S. Rana will attend the inaugural session, which will be presided over by IEASA president Mohan Patel.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Siddhartha Academy president M. Rajayya, secretary P. Lakshman Rao, joint secretary N. Lalitha Prasad and Academic Advisor L.K. Mohan Rao will also attend.

📰 P.B. Siddhartha College to host international seminar on Viksit Bharat from November 19

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 09:23:43 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Parvathaneni Brahmayya Siddhartha College of Arts and Science, Vijayawada, will host a three-day international seminar on “Viksit Bharat @2047” from November 19 in collaboration with the Indian Economics and Allied Sciences Association (IEASA).

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: At a press conference on Tuesday, college Principal Meka Ramesh, Director Vemuri Babu Rao, Dean and conference convener Rajesh C. The inaugural session will be held at PVP Siddhartha College of Information Technology, while the subsequent sessions over the three days will be conducted at P.B. Siddhartha College of Arts and Science. Adani Group CEO (Skills and Education) Robin Bhowmik, Canara Bank General Manager and Circle Head Devaraj R. and Symboyzia Group Director G.S. Rana will attend the inaugural session, which will be presided over by IEASA president Mohan Patel.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Siddhartha Academy president M. Rajayya, secretary P. Lakshman Rao, joint secretary N. Lalitha Prasad and Academic Advisor L.K. Mohan Rao will also attend.

articles.title: Naidu seeks immediate Central assistance to cope with damages caused by two cyclones
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The successive weather systems, ‘Arnab’ and ‘Murasu’, have inflicted losses estimated at over ₹7,000 crore, he informs Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman; he also urges release of funds for developing infrastructure for the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has sought immediate financial assistance from the Union government to help the State cope with the damage caused by two successive cyclones (Arnab and Murasu), which inflicted losses estimated at over ₹7,000 crore. During a meeting with Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi on November 17, 2026 (Tuesday), Mr. Naidu explained the impact of the two cyclones on agriculture, power infrastructure and other sectors, and urged her to extend immediate financial support. He said crops nearing harvest had been damaged, leaving farmers in distress. Despite the impact of El Niño, the State had supplied irrigation water to some regions through the Pattiseema project to help the farmers, but the successive cyclones caused extensive crop losses, the Chief Minister said. Coastal infrastructure, particularly the power distribution network, suffered considerable damage. The Chief Minister said Central teams had visited the State to assess the damage and were expected to submit their reports soon. Immediate assistance, even before completion of the assessment process, would provide some financial relief to the State, he said. The Chief Minister also discussed region-wise development plans for Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati. Mr. Naidu recalled that Ms. Sitharaman had laid the stone for the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub, and sought the release of funds for developing supporting infrastructure, including rural roads, irrigation facilities and drip irrigation systems. He also sought additional Central assistance for the Visakhapatnam Economic Region (VER), saying it was witnessing rapid growth and that further support would help extend the benefits of development to the people. The Chief Minister briefed the Finance Minister about the recent CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam, including the investment proposals and discussions held during the two-day event.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: State Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav, MPs and senior Finance Department officials attended the meeting.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 Naidu seeks immediate Central assistance to cope with damages caused by two cyclones

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 09:22:38 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The successive weather systems, ‘Arnab’ and ‘Murasu’, have inflicted losses estimated at over ₹7,000 crore, he informs Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman; he also urges release of funds for developing infrastructure for the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has sought immediate financial assistance from the Union government to help the State cope with the damage caused by two successive cyclones (Arnab and Murasu), which inflicted losses estimated at over ₹7,000 crore. During a meeting with Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi on November 17, 2026 (Tuesday), Mr. Naidu explained the impact of the two cyclones on agriculture, power infrastructure and other sectors, and urged her to extend immediate financial support. He said crops nearing harvest had been damaged, leaving farmers in distress. Despite the impact of El Niño, the State had supplied irrigation water to some regions through the Pattiseema project to help the farmers, but the successive cyclones caused extensive crop losses, the Chief Minister said. Coastal infrastructure, particularly the power distribution network, suffered considerable damage. The Chief Minister said Central teams had visited the State to assess the damage and were expected to submit their reports soon. Immediate assistance, even before completion of the assessment process, would provide some financial relief to the State, he said. The Chief Minister also discussed region-wise development plans for Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati. Mr. Naidu recalled that Ms. Sitharaman had laid the stone for the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub, and sought the release of funds for developing supporting infrastructure, including rural roads, irrigation facilities and drip irrigation systems. He also sought additional Central assistance for the Visakhapatnam Economic Region (VER), saying it was witnessing rapid growth and that further support would help extend the benefits of development to the people. The Chief Minister briefed the Finance Minister about the recent CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam, including the investment proposals and discussions held during the two-day event.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: State Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav, MPs and senior Finance Department officials attended the meeting.

• 1. Core Context & Background: The successive weather systems, ‘Arnab’ and ‘Murasu’, have inflicted losses estimated at over ₹7,000 crore, he informs Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman; he also urges release of funds for developing infrastructure for the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has sought immediate financial assistance from the Union government to help the State cope with the damage caused by two successive cyclones (Arnab and Murasu), which inflicted losses estimated at over ₹7,000 crore. During a meeting with Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi on November 17, 2026 (Tuesday), Mr. Naidu explained the impact of the two cyclones on agriculture, power infrastructure and other sectors, and urged her to extend immediate financial support. He said crops nearing harvest had been damaged, leaving farmers in distress. Despite the impact of El Niño, the State had supplied irrigation water to some regions through the Pattiseema project to help the farmers, but the successive cyclones caused extensive crop losses, the Chief Minister said. Coastal infrastructure, particularly the power distribution network, suffered considerable damage. The Chief Minister said Central teams had visited the State to assess the damage and were expected to submit their reports soon. Immediate assistance, even before completion of the assessment process, would provide some financial relief to the State, he said. The Chief Minister also discussed region-wise development plans for Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati. Mr. Naidu recalled that Ms. Sitharaman had laid the stone for the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub, and sought the release of funds for developing supporting infrastructure, including rural roads, irrigation facilities and drip irrigation systems. He also sought additional Central assistance for the Visakhapatnam Economic Region (VER), saying it was witnessing rapid growth and that further support would help extend the benefits of development to the people. The Chief Minister briefed the Finance Minister about the recent CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam, including the investment proposals and discussions held during the two-day event.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: State Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav, MPs and senior Finance Department officials attended the meeting.

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Congress on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) accused the Union government of fuelling inflation through its “economic mismanagement and anti-people policies” and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi remained preoccupied with politics rather than addressing the economic distress faced by households and businesses. Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh cited a survey which found that, for 61% of families across the country, monthly household expenditure had risen by more than 20% over the past year. While 74% of respondents were cutting back on non-essential spending, 50% had reduced purchases of essential goods, he said. Citing the survey, Mr. Ramesh said prices of ghee and edible oils had risen by 75%, vegetables by 73%, cereals by 71%, milk and dairy products by 65%, and pulses by 62%. He also claimed that 200 garment factories had shut down in Noida over the past year, citing the impact of U.S. tariffs, high input costs, and government apathy. He said the closures reflected the wider distress in the textile industry. “People’s plates are shrinking, and factories are being locked down. Yet, the Prime Minister’s only concern remains politics,” he said on X, accusing the government of failing to acknowledge people’s hardships or offer relief.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Indian National Congress / national government / Bharatiya Janata Party / Narendra Modi / inflation and deflation

articles.title: India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: PM’s adviser
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that India or any other country could not dictate terms over deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s return home. Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government. Talking to reporters at the Bangladesh Secretariat, Mr. Zahed said, “Bangladesh is now an independent, sovereign state standing on firm legal ground and it will reject any unjust terms.” The premier’s Adviser, however, said he did not believe India would attach conditions to returning Hasina. On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Hasina's extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly. He further said: “India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh." Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal convicted Hasina in November 2025 of crimes against humanity for her role in the crackdown on protesters during the July-August 2024 uprising. Tried in absentia, she was sentenced to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another. Hasina has rejected the charges and the proceedings. In a report last week, BBC Bangla said unnamed Indian officials indicated that New Delhi set two main conditions to facilitate Hasina’s return amid Dhaka’s repeated insistence on her extradition under a bilateral treaty despite her repeated stated plan to return home voluntarily to face the legal procedure.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The report said that “under the conditions, India wanted Bangladesh Army to directly receive Hasina either via a military flight to Delhi or at a land border crossing”.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (17 NOV)

📰 India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: PM’s adviser

📌 Published: 17 Nov 2026, 09:07:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Information Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) said that India or any other country could not dictate terms over deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s return home. Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government. Talking to reporters at the Bangladesh Secretariat, Mr. Zahed said, “Bangladesh is now an independent, sovereign state standing on firm legal ground and it will reject any unjust terms.” The premier’s Adviser, however, said he did not believe India would attach conditions to returning Hasina. On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Hasina's extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly. He further said: “India desires a positive, constructive and forward-looking relationship with Bangladesh." Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal convicted Hasina in November 2025 of crimes against humanity for her role in the crackdown on protesters during the July-August 2024 uprising. Tried in absentia, she was sentenced to death on one charge and life imprisonment on another. Hasina has rejected the charges and the proceedings. In a report last week, BBC Bangla said unnamed Indian officials indicated that New Delhi set two main conditions to facilitate Hasina’s return amid Dhaka’s repeated insistence on her extradition under a bilateral treaty despite her repeated stated plan to return home voluntarily to face the legal procedure.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The report said that “under the conditions, India wanted Bangladesh Army to directly receive Hasina either via a military flight to Delhi or at a land border crossing”.

Bilateral (Adjective)
द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत।
✓ Syn: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way
International (Adjective)
अंतरराष्ट्रीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'International' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Constructive (Adjective)
रचनात्मक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Constructive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Imprisonment (Adjective)
कैद होना — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Imprisonment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

A. Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

D. The author contends that 'India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing the country in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government." (Hinglish Arth: अगस्त 2024 में छात्र नेतृत्व वाले विद्रोह के बाद देश से भागने के बाद से हसीना भारत में रह रही हैं, जिससे उनकी सरकार गिर गई थी।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "India cannot dictate terms on Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: PM’s adviser"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The report said that “under the conditions, India wanted Bangladesh Army to directly receive Hasina either via a military flight to Delhi or at a...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The report said that “under the conditions, India wanted Bangladesh Army to directly receive Hasina either via a military flight to Delhi or at a..." fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Quad is a ‘trusted partnership’ delivering solutions, says PM Modi

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed for New Delhi after concluding his two-day visit to the Philippines, during which he attended the ASEAN-India Summit, the East Asia Summit and a meeting of the Quad leaders. Mr. Modi also met Philippine President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr., and the two leaders discussed ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in defence, security, trade and investment. The Prime Minister also discussed regional and global issues of mutual interest with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand on the sidelines of the visit. Leaders of ‌the four-nation Quad grouping ⁠strongly oppose any destabilising or ‌unilateral actions that seek ‌to ‌change ⁠the status ⁠quo, including by force or coercion, which ‌escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and ‌stability, a joint statement said. The leaders also ‌expressed grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary ‌export restrictions, the statement added after their ⁠meeting in Manila. The Quad grouping, following its meeting in Manila, announced the ‘Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration’ which is “ a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness” “In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer,” the statement added. In a joint press release following the Quad meeting in Manila, the group said that it “affirms the importance of the AI Accelerator, announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta.” “The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific,” it added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed ways to strengthen cooperation and exchanged views on regional and global developments with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand in separate bilateral meetings in the Philippines.
