🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (16 NOV)

📰 India and Egypt form working group to explore trade deal contours

📌 Published: 16 Nov 2026, 10:46:42 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: India and Egypt have agreed to establish a joint working group to explore the Terms of Reference (ToR) for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement between the two countries, the government announced on Monday (November 16, 2026).

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: During his ongoing visit to Egypt, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal co-chaired, along with Egypt’s Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid Saleh, the 7th session of the India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital. This was the first time this JTC has been convened at the ministerial level. “As a key outcome of the 7th Joint Trade Committee meeting, both Ministers agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries,” the government said in a release. The release also said that both sides reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, with a target of $12 billion. “Egypt’s proximity to the Suez Canal and its connectivity with African, Arab and European markets make it a valuable partner for export-oriented manufacturing and regional supply chains,” the release said. “India, in turn, offers Egyptian investors and exporters a large and dynamic market, increasingly competitive infrastructure and opportunities for technology and production partnerships,” it added. The committee also reviewed the growth in India-Egypt trade, which increased by 35% to $6.5 billion in 2025-26. Trade during the first half of the current financial year (April-September 2026) also stood at a little more than $5 billion, up 65% over its level in the same period of 2025. Piyush Goyal in Egypt: Both sides to discuss increasing cooperation in infra, manufacturing, logistics

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: India, U.S. agreed on preferential market access for Indian goods in America: Goyal

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Developing countries call for developed nations to lead emissions cuts and climate finance efforts

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Developing countries have called on developed nations to take the lead in achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 and net-negative emissions by 2045, as divergent positions emerged in the draft cover text at the ongoing COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye. Net zero refers to balancing the amount of carbon dioxide emitted with the amount removed from the atmosphere. Several developed countries have set 2050 targets for achieving net-zero emissions, while major developing economies such as India and China have committed to targets of 2070 and 2060, respectively. The positions of developing countries are largely represented by coalitions such as the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), which includes India, the Arab Group, the African Group and the Least Developed Countries (LDCs). Developed-country positions are primarily represented by the European Union, the United Kingdom and Japan. The United States has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement. The draft cover text also includes a proposal asking developing countries to contribute voluntarily towards climate finance. This funding is intended to help countries adapt to a fossil-fuel-free economy and address losses and damage caused by climate change. Under the UN climate framework, developed countries, which bear greater historical responsibility for accumulated carbon emissions, are expected to support developing countries through finance and technology as they pursue lower-emission development pathways. Developing countries have also called for the elimination of measures such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) by the end of 2027. The mechanism imposes a tariff on certain imports, including steel, based on the carbon emissions generated during production. Developing countries argue that such measures disadvantage their industries, which often have lower production costs but higher emissions. Another proposal in the draft concerns a target to source 35% of energy use from electricity by 2035. Some countries have called for there to be no obligation to meet this goal, which was proposed by the COP31 presidency. COP31 president of negotiations Chris Bowens said the first draft was intended to incorporate proposals from all parties, acknowledging that countries would disagree on certain elements. He said the draft had been released early to ensure transparency and reflect the range of positions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at activist group 350.org, called for a transition towards renewable energy and electrification, supported by adequate funding. He said the credibility of the climate negotiations depended on leadership in moving away from fossil fuels.

hinglishTracks.en: Developing countries call for developed nations to lead emissions cuts and climate finance efforts
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — विकासशील देश विकसित देशों से उत्सर्जन में कटौती और जलवायु वित्त प्रयासों का नेतृत्व करने का आह्वान करते हैं। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Development' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Developing countries have called on developed nations to take the lead in achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 and net-negative emissions by 2045, as divergent positions emerged in the draft cover text at the ongoing COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — विकासशील देशों ने विकसित देशों से 2030 तक शुद्ध-शून्य उत्सर्जन और 2045 तक शुद्ध-नकारात्मक उत्सर्जन प्राप्त करने का नेतृत्व करने का आह्वान किया है, क्योंकि अंताल्या, तुर्किये में चल रही COP31 जलवायु वार्ता में मसौदा कवर पाठ में अलग-अलग स्थिति सामने आई है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Development' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Net zero refers to balancing the amount of carbon dioxide emitted with the amount removed from the atmosphere.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — नेट ज़ीरो का तात्पर्य उत्सर्जित कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड की मात्रा को वायुमंडल से निकाली गई मात्रा के साथ संतुलित करना है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Several developed countries have set 2050 targets for achieving net-zero emissions, while major developing economies such as India and China have committed to targets of 2070 and 2060, respectively.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — कई विकसित देशों ने शुद्ध-शून्य उत्सर्जन प्राप्त करने के लिए 2050 लक्ष्य निर्धारित किए हैं, जबकि भारत और चीन जैसी प्रमुख विकासशील अर्थव्यवस्थाएं क्रमशः 2070 और 2060 के लक्ष्य के लिए प्रतिबद्ध हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Development' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: The positions of developing countries are largely represented by coalitions such as the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), which includes India, the Arab Group, the African Group and the Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — विकासशील देशों की स्थिति का प्रतिनिधित्व बड़े पैमाने पर समान विचारधारा वाले विकासशील देशों (एलएमडीसी) जैसे गठबंधनों द्वारा किया जाता है, जिसमें भारत, अरब समूह, अफ्रीकी समूह और सबसे कम विकसित देश (एलडीसी) शामिल हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Development' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Developed-country positions are primarily represented by the European Union, the United Kingdom and Japan.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — विकसित देशों की स्थिति का प्रतिनिधित्व मुख्य रूप से यूरोपीय संघ, यूनाइटेड किंगडम और जापान द्वारा किया जाता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Development' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: The United States has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका पेरिस समझौते से हट गया है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The draft cover text also includes a proposal asking developing countries to contribute voluntarily towards climate finance.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — ड्राफ्ट कवर टेक्स्ट में एक प्रस्ताव भी शामिल है जिसमें विकासशील देशों से जलवायु वित्त के लिए स्वेच्छा से योगदान करने के लिए कहा गया है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Development' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: This funding is intended to help countries adapt to a fossil-fuel-free economy and address losses and damage caused by climate change.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — इस फंडिंग का उद्देश्य देशों को जीवाश्म-ईंधन-मुक्त अर्थव्यवस्था को अपनाने में मदद करना और जलवायु परिवर्तन से होने वाले नुकसान और क्षति का समाधान करना है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Under the UN climate framework, developed countries, which bear greater historical responsibility for accumulated carbon emissions, are expected to support developing countries through finance and technology as they pursue lower-emission development pathways.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — संयुक्त राष्ट्र जलवायु ढांचे के तहत, विकसित देश, जो संचित कार्बन उत्सर्जन के लिए अधिक ऐतिहासिक जिम्मेदारी वहन करते हैं, से अपेक्षा की जाती है कि वे वित्त और प्रौद्योगिकी के माध्यम से विकासशील देशों का समर्थन करें क्योंकि वे कम उत्सर्जन वाले विकास पथ अपनाते हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Responsibility' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Responsibility' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Developing countries have also called for the elimination of measures such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) by the end of 2027.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — विकासशील देशों ने 2027 के अंत तक यूरोपीय संघ के कार्बन सीमा समायोजन तंत्र (सीबीएएम) जैसे उपायों को खत्म करने का भी आह्वान किया है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Development' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: The mechanism imposes a tariff on certain imports, including steel, based on the carbon emissions generated during production.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यह तंत्र उत्पादन के दौरान उत्पन्न कार्बन उत्सर्जन के आधार पर स्टील सहित कुछ आयातों पर टैरिफ लगाता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Developing countries argue that such measures disadvantage their industries, which often have lower production costs but higher emissions.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — विकासशील देशों का तर्क है कि ऐसे उपायों से उनके उद्योगों को नुकसान होता है, जिनकी उत्पादन लागत अक्सर कम होती है लेकिन उत्सर्जन अधिक होता है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Development' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: Another proposal in the draft concerns a target to source 35% of energy use from electricity by 2035.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — मसौदे में एक अन्य प्रस्ताव 2035 तक ऊर्जा उपयोग का 35% बिजली से प्राप्त करने के लक्ष्य से संबंधित है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Electrification' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Electrification' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Some countries have called for there to be no obligation to meet this goal, which was proposed by the COP31 presidency.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — कुछ देशों ने इस लक्ष्य को पूरा करने के लिए कोई बाध्यता नहीं रखने का आह्वान किया है, जिसे COP31 प्रेसीडेंसी द्वारा प्रस्तावित किया गया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: COP31 president of negotiations Chris Bowens said the first draft was intended to incorporate proposals from all parties, acknowledging that countries would disagree on certain elements.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — COP31 वार्ता के अध्यक्ष क्रिस बोवेन्स ने कहा कि पहले मसौदे का उद्देश्य सभी पक्षों के प्रस्तावों को शामिल करना था, यह स्वीकार करते हुए कि देश कुछ तत्वों पर असहमत होंगे।।

hinglishTracks.en: He said the draft had been released early to ensure transparency and reflect the range of positions.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — उन्होंने कहा कि पारदर्शिता सुनिश्चित करने और पदों की सीमा को प्रतिबिंबित करने के लिए मसौदा जल्दी जारी किया गया था।।

hinglishTracks.en: Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at activist group 350.org, called for a transition towards renewable energy and electrification, supported by adequate funding.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — एक्टिविस्ट ग्रुप 350.org में राजनीतिक रणनीति के प्रमुख एंड्रियास सीबर ने पर्याप्त फंडिंग द्वारा समर्थित नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा और विद्युतीकरण की दिशा में बदलाव का आह्वान किया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Electrification' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Electrification' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: He said the credibility of the climate negotiations depended on leadership in moving away from fossil fuels.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — उन्होंने कहा कि जलवायु वार्ता की विश्वसनीयता जीवाश्म ईंधन से दूर जाने के नेतृत्व पर निर्भर करती है।।

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (16 NOV)

📰 Divergent positions mark draft text of COP31 under way in Turkiye

📌 Published: 16 Nov 2026, 10:42:58 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Developing countries call for developed nations to lead emissions cuts and climate finance efforts

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Developing countries have called on developed nations to take the lead in achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 and net-negative emissions by 2045, as divergent positions emerged in the draft cover text at the ongoing COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye. Net zero refers to balancing the amount of carbon dioxide emitted with the amount removed from the atmosphere. Several developed countries have set 2050 targets for achieving net-zero emissions, while major developing economies such as India and China have committed to targets of 2070 and 2060, respectively. The positions of developing countries are largely represented by coalitions such as the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), which includes India, the Arab Group, the African Group and the Least Developed Countries (LDCs). Developed-country positions are primarily represented by the European Union, the United Kingdom and Japan. The United States has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement. The draft cover text also includes a proposal asking developing countries to contribute voluntarily towards climate finance. This funding is intended to help countries adapt to a fossil-fuel-free economy and address losses and damage caused by climate change. Under the UN climate framework, developed countries, which bear greater historical responsibility for accumulated carbon emissions, are expected to support developing countries through finance and technology as they pursue lower-emission development pathways. Developing countries have also called for the elimination of measures such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) by the end of 2027. The mechanism imposes a tariff on certain imports, including steel, based on the carbon emissions generated during production. Developing countries argue that such measures disadvantage their industries, which often have lower production costs but higher emissions. Another proposal in the draft concerns a target to source 35% of energy use from electricity by 2035. Some countries have called for there to be no obligation to meet this goal, which was proposed by the COP31 presidency. COP31 president of negotiations Chris Bowens said the first draft was intended to incorporate proposals from all parties, acknowledging that countries would disagree on certain elements. He said the draft had been released early to ensure transparency and reflect the range of positions.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at activist group 350.org, called for a transition towards renewable energy and electrification, supported by adequate funding. He said the credibility of the climate negotiations depended on leadership in moving away from fossil fuels.

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Developing countries call for developed nations to lead emissions cuts and climate finance efforts
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Developing countries have called on developed nations to take the lead in achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 and net-negative emissions by 2045, as divergent positions emerged in the draft cover text at the ongoing COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye. Net zero refers to balancing the amount of carbon dioxide emitted with the amount removed from the atmosphere. Several developed countries have set 2050 targets for achieving net-zero emissions, while major developing economies such as India and China have committed to targets of 2070 and 2060, respectively. The positions of developing countries are largely represented by coalitions such as the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), which includes India, the Arab Group, the African Group and the Least Developed Countries (LDCs). Developed-country positions are primarily represented by the European Union, the United Kingdom and Japan. The United States has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement. The draft cover text also includes a proposal asking developing countries to contribute voluntarily towards climate finance. This funding is intended to help countries adapt to a fossil-fuel-free economy and address losses and damage caused by climate change. Under the UN climate framework, developed countries, which bear greater historical responsibility for accumulated carbon emissions, are expected to support developing countries through finance and technology as they pursue lower-emission development pathways. Developing countries have also called for the elimination of measures such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) by the end of 2027. The mechanism imposes a tariff on certain imports, including steel, based on the carbon emissions generated during production. Developing countries argue that such measures disadvantage their industries, which often have lower production costs but higher emissions. Another proposal in the draft concerns a target to source 35% of energy use from electricity by 2035. Some countries have called for there to be no obligation to meet this goal, which was proposed by the COP31 presidency. COP31 president of negotiations Chris Bowens said the first draft was intended to incorporate proposals from all parties, acknowledging that countries would disagree on certain elements. He said the draft had been released early to ensure transparency and reflect the range of positions.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at activist group 350.org, called for a transition towards renewable energy and electrification, supported by adequate funding. He said the credibility of the climate negotiations depended on leadership in moving away from fossil fuels.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The U SS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the West Asia, once again bringing the total number of U.S. aircraft carriers in the West Asia to three — an unusually high number. A U.S. official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military operations, on Monday (November 16, 2026) confirmed the carrier’s arrival in the region. It brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East as President Donald Trump has kept his options open during the more than 8-month-old Iran war. The Roosevelt, along with its accompanying strike force, left San Diego in September. The Theodore Roosevelt joins the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as scores of smaller navy ships, that are in the region maintaining a blockade of Iranian shipping. The H.W. Bush arrived in the region in April while the George Washington arrived in August.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the Navy, the flotilla in the Arabian Sea now includes three aircraft carriers as well as 13 destroyers, two cruisers and a littoral combat ship.

articles.title: After Yemen setback, Saudi Arabia replaces military commander
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Saudi Arabia replaced the commander overseeing its coalition against Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthis ‌on Monday (November 16, 2026) after Riyadh’s Yemeni allies were forced to withdraw from swathes of territory in ​a major setback for their campaign against the group. The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group. After gaining ground in a counter-attack in October, the Yemeni government said on Sunday (November 15, 2026) it was withdrawing from ‌areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a global shipping artery, to focus on defending its base of operations in Aden, a port city on the southern coast. People in the Yemeni military ‌said on Monday (November 16, 2026) the Houthis had advanced to the southern coastal area of Khor Omairh, ‌some ⁠100 km (62 miles) west of Aden and were 25 km (16 miles) from government lines at Qawah, ⁠another coastal area. A royal decree issued by Saudi Arabia’s King Salman spelt out changes to the command of the Saudi-led coalition. The existing commander, Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad Al-Salman, was appointed as adviser to the defence minister for military affairs, while Chief of ​the General Staff General Fayyad Al-Ruwaili was assigned ‌the additional role of commanding the joint forces, Saudi state media reported. Two Western diplomats linked the change directly to battlefield developments in Yemen and the Houthi advance. The Saudi government media office didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports and ‌oil facilities since the Yemen war restarted.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on ​Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping have enhanced Iran’s position in the wider Middle East conflict.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (16 NOV)

📰 After Yemen setback, Saudi Arabia replaces military commander

📌 Published: 16 Nov 2026, 10:15:13 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Saudi Arabia replaced the commander overseeing its coalition against Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthis ‌on Monday (November 16, 2026) after Riyadh’s Yemeni allies were forced to withdraw from swathes of territory in ​a major setback for their campaign against the group. The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group. After gaining ground in a counter-attack in October, the Yemeni government said on Sunday (November 15, 2026) it was withdrawing from ‌areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a global shipping artery, to focus on defending its base of operations in Aden, a port city on the southern coast. People in the Yemeni military ‌said on Monday (November 16, 2026) the Houthis had advanced to the southern coastal area of Khor Omairh, ‌some ⁠100 km (62 miles) west of Aden and were 25 km (16 miles) from government lines at Qawah, ⁠another coastal area. A royal decree issued by Saudi Arabia’s King Salman spelt out changes to the command of the Saudi-led coalition. The existing commander, Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad Al-Salman, was appointed as adviser to the defence minister for military affairs, while Chief of ​the General Staff General Fayyad Al-Ruwaili was assigned ‌the additional role of commanding the joint forces, Saudi state media reported. Two Western diplomats linked the change directly to battlefield developments in Yemen and the Houthi advance. The Saudi government media office didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports and ‌oil facilities since the Yemen war restarted.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on ​Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping have enhanced Iran’s position in the wider Middle East conflict.

articles.title: Israeli opposition chiefs denounce Netanyahu over ‘attempted coup’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced Monday (November 16, 2026) an "attempted coup" following press reports that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election. "As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear: This wasn't an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup," wrote Yair Lapid on X, who headed the opposition in the previous legislature and co-chairs the Beyachad list. Israel's Channel 12 reported Sunday (November 15, 2026) that on the eve of the October 27 election, Mr. Netanyahu's chief of staff Ido Norden had phoned in a complaint to the police about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party. Mr. Norden reportedly pointed the police to a purported intelligence source -- a former employee of Mr. Netanyahu's office -- who provided information that led to the arrest of three Raam members. The three men were later released when the police determined that the information was unfounded. Mr. Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats. His Likud party issued a statement denying the latest allegations. The Israeli newspaper Haaretz also reported that David Zini, head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, sought to wiretap leaders of the other Arab slate, the Joint List, but the attorney general turned down his request due to lack of evidence. Following the report, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen also denounced an "attempted coup by Netanyahu". "If the findings are confirmed, this is a criminal mechanism that operated from the heart of government to rig the election results. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable, including Netanyahu," he wrote on X.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Raam's number two, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent investigation.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (16 NOV)

📰 Israeli opposition chiefs denounce Netanyahu over ‘attempted coup’

📌 Published: 16 Nov 2026, 10:05:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced Monday (November 16, 2026) an "attempted coup" following press reports that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election. "As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear: This wasn't an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup," wrote Yair Lapid on X, who headed the opposition in the previous legislature and co-chairs the Beyachad list. Israel's Channel 12 reported Sunday (November 15, 2026) that on the eve of the October 27 election, Mr. Netanyahu's chief of staff Ido Norden had phoned in a complaint to the police about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party. Mr. Norden reportedly pointed the police to a purported intelligence source -- a former employee of Mr. Netanyahu's office -- who provided information that led to the arrest of three Raam members. The three men were later released when the police determined that the information was unfounded. Mr. Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats. His Likud party issued a statement denying the latest allegations. The Israeli newspaper Haaretz also reported that David Zini, head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, sought to wiretap leaders of the other Arab slate, the Joint List, but the attorney general turned down his request due to lack of evidence. Following the report, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen also denounced an "attempted coup by Netanyahu". "If the findings are confirmed, this is a criminal mechanism that operated from the heart of government to rig the election results. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable, including Netanyahu," he wrote on X.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Raam's number two, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent investigation.

articles.title: How does India address service outages?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Does Indian law require Microsoft to have reported the recent outage that affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite? What rules apply in such situations and what are their shortcomings in the present form? How are cloud companies accountable in other countries? What are Indian customers’ options?

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: From November 12 to 13, an as-yet unspecified problem with Microsoft infrastructure affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite Microsoft 365 worldwide, including its Outlook email service. Microsoft apologised during the outage and attributed the incident to a fault in an upgrade of its network capacity, although more precise details are still expected. In India, among consequences in various sectors, IndiGo and Akasa Air alerted passengers of disruptions to their email support while Air India rerouted its email. The incident raises larger questions about whether companies providing services on which lakhs of people depend are required to account for such failures in India. First, the directions issued by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) on April 28, 2022, under the Information Technology Act, 2000, require companies to report cyber incidents within six hours. The directions cover attacks and intrusions but not outages caused by technical faults. Still, CERT-In can call for information under Section 70B(6) of the IT Act to seek an explanation from Microsoft. The second is the Reserve Bank of India’s directions on managing risks in outsourcing, issued on November 28, 2025. They carry forward rules on outsourced IT services that first took effect on October 1, 2023. A bank buying cloud services must assess its dependence on the supplier and have an exit strategy. If the arrangement fails, the RBI can hold the bank responsible and the bank can seek an explanation from Microsoft under its agreement. The third is the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. The Act defines a personal data breach to include an accidental “loss of access to personal data”. Under Rules set to come into effect in May 2027, data breaches must be reported to the Data Protection Board and to each affected person. Failure to report could attract a penalty of up to ₹200 crore. The onus is on the organisation that collected the data, and the organisation is Microsoft’s customer, even though the data sits on Microsoft’s servers. While Indian law does not require a minimum threshold of harm to report a breach, it is unclear whether a temporary outage constitutes a “loss of access” and thus a breach. If yes, a company must report the outage; if not, the company need not report, even if customers complained throughout the day. Europe’s regulators count even a temporary loss of access as a breach to be logged, but only demand a report if people are put at risk. A faulty update to Falcon Sensor, a security programme sold by CrowdStrike, caused some 8.5 million Windows computers worldwide to crash on July 19, 2024. The machines showed a blue error screen, known as the “Blue Screen of Death”, and kept crashing until the faulty file was removed. IndiGo cancelled 283 flights. This week, the computers did not crash as the failure was in Microsoft’s own data centres. Following the incident, CERT-In issued a “critical” advisory and Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw said his Ministry was in touch with Microsoft.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The European Union and the U.K. have placed the biggest tech vendors directly under financial regulators’ watch. The EU’s financial supervisors named 19 such companies under its Digital Operational Resilience Act on November 18, 2025, which includes Microsoft and Tata Consultancy Services. Thus, an Indian company already reports to European supervisors.

(Hinglish Arth: इस प्रकार, एक भारतीय कंपनी पहले से ही यूरोपीय पर्यवेक्षकों को रिपोर्ट करती है।)

hinglishTracks.en: Does Indian law require Microsoft to have reported the recent outage that affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite?
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — क्या भारतीय कानून के अनुसार माइक्रोसॉफ्ट को हालिया आउटेज की रिपोर्ट करने की आवश्यकता है जिससे ग्राहकों की उत्पादकता सूट तक पहुंचने की क्षमता प्रभावित हुई है?। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Productivity' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: उत्पादकता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Productivity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: What rules apply in such situations and what are their shortcomings in the present form?
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — ऐसी स्थितियों में कौन से नियम लागू होते हैं और वर्तमान स्वरूप में उनकी क्या कमियाँ हैं?।

hinglishTracks.en: How are cloud companies accountable in other countries?
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — क्लाउड कंपनियाँ अन्य देशों में कैसे जवाबदेह हैं?। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Accountability' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता। इसके Synonyms हैं: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability और Antonyms हैं: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility।

hinglishTracks.en: What are Indian customers’ options?
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — भारतीय ग्राहकों के पास क्या विकल्प हैं?।

hinglishTracks.en: From November 12 to 13, an as-yet unspecified problem with Microsoft infrastructure affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite Microsoft 365 worldwide, including its Outlook email service.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — 12 से 13 नवंबर तक, Microsoft बुनियादी ढांचे के साथ एक अनिर्दिष्ट समस्या ने ग्राहकों की आउटलुक ईमेल सेवा सहित दुनिया भर में इसके उत्पादकता सूट Microsoft 365 तक पहुंचने की क्षमता को प्रभावित किया।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Productivity' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: उत्पादकता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Productivity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: Microsoft apologised during the outage and attributed the incident to a fault in an upgrade of its network capacity, although more precise details are still expected.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — माइक्रोसॉफ्ट ने आउटेज के दौरान माफी मांगी और इस घटना के लिए अपनी नेटवर्क क्षमता के अपग्रेड में गलती को जिम्मेदार ठहराया, हालांकि अधिक सटीक विवरण अभी भी अपेक्षित हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: In India, among consequences in various sectors, IndiGo and Akasa Air alerted passengers of disruptions to their email support while Air India rerouted its email.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — भारत में, विभिन्न क्षेत्रों में परिणामों के बीच, इंडिगो और अकासा एयर ने यात्रियों को उनके ईमेल समर्थन में व्यवधान के बारे में सचेत किया, जबकि एयर इंडिया ने अपने ईमेल का रूट बदल दिया।।

hinglishTracks.en: The incident raises larger questions about whether companies providing services on which lakhs of people depend are required to account for such failures in India.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — यह घटना इस बात पर बड़ा सवाल उठाती है कि क्या सेवाएं प्रदान करने वाली कंपनियां जिन पर लाखों लोग निर्भर हैं, उन्हें भारत में ऐसी विफलताओं के लिए जिम्मेदार ठहराया जाना चाहिए।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Accountability' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता। इसके Synonyms हैं: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability और Antonyms हैं: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility।

hinglishTracks.en: First, the directions issued by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) on April 28, 2022, under the Information Technology Act, 2000, require companies to report cyber incidents within six hours.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — सबसे पहले, सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी अधिनियम, 2000 के तहत 28 अप्रैल, 2022 को भारतीय कंप्यूटर आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया टीम (सीईआरटी-इन) द्वारा जारी निर्देशों के अनुसार, कंपनियों को छह घंटे के भीतर साइबर घटनाओं की रिपोर्ट करने की आवश्यकता होती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The directions cover attacks and intrusions but not outages caused by technical faults.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — निर्देश हमलों और घुसपैठ को कवर करते हैं लेकिन तकनीकी दोषों के कारण होने वाली क्षति को नहीं।।

hinglishTracks.en: Still, CERT-In can call for information under Section 70B(6) of the IT Act to seek an explanation from Microsoft.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — फिर भी, CERT-In Microsoft से स्पष्टीकरण मांगने के लिए IT अधिनियम की धारा 70B(6) के तहत जानकारी मांग सकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The second is the Reserve Bank of India’s directions on managing risks in outsourcing, issued on November 28, 2025.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — दूसरा आउटसोर्सिंग में जोखिमों के प्रबंधन पर भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक के निर्देश हैं, जो 28 नवंबर, 2025 को जारी किए गए थे।।

hinglishTracks.en: They carry forward rules on outsourced IT services that first took effect on October 1, 2023.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — वे आउटसोर्स आईटी सेवाओं पर नियमों को आगे बढ़ाते हैं जो पहली बार 1 अक्टूबर, 2023 को प्रभावी हुए।।

hinglishTracks.en: A bank buying cloud services must assess its dependence on the supplier and have an exit strategy.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — क्लाउड सेवाएं खरीदने वाले बैंक को आपूर्तिकर्ता पर अपनी निर्भरता का आकलन करना चाहिए और बाहर निकलने की रणनीति बनानी चाहिए।।

hinglishTracks.en: If the arrangement fails, the RBI can hold the bank responsible and the bank can seek an explanation from Microsoft under its agreement.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — यदि व्यवस्था विफल हो जाती है, तो आरबीआई बैंक को जिम्मेदार ठहरा सकता है और बैंक अपने समझौते के तहत माइक्रोसॉफ्ट से स्पष्टीकरण मांग सकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The third is the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — तीसरा है डिजिटल पर्सनल डेटा प्रोटेक्शन एक्ट, 2023।।

hinglishTracks.en: The Act defines a personal data breach to include an accidental “loss of access to personal data”.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — अधिनियम व्यक्तिगत डेटा उल्लंघन को परिभाषित करता है जिसमें आकस्मिक "व्यक्तिगत डेटा तक पहुंच की हानि" शामिल है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Under Rules set to come into effect in May 2027, data breaches must be reported to the Data Protection Board and to each affected person.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — मई 2027 में लागू होने वाले नियमों के तहत, डेटा उल्लंघनों की सूचना डेटा संरक्षण बोर्ड और प्रत्येक प्रभावित व्यक्ति को दी जानी चाहिए।।

hinglishTracks.en: Failure to report could attract a penalty of up to ₹200 crore.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — रिपोर्ट न करने पर ₹200 करोड़ तक का जुर्माना लग सकता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The onus is on the organisation that collected the data, and the organisation is Microsoft’s customer, even though the data sits on Microsoft’s servers.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — जिम्मेदारी उस संगठन पर है जिसने डेटा एकत्र किया है, और संगठन Microsoft का ग्राहक है, भले ही डेटा Microsoft के सर्वर पर मौजूद हो।।

hinglishTracks.en: While Indian law does not require a minimum threshold of harm to report a breach, it is unclear whether a temporary outage constitutes a “loss of access” and thus a breach.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — हालांकि भारतीय कानून में किसी उल्लंघन की रिपोर्ट करने के लिए नुकसान की न्यूनतम सीमा की आवश्यकता नहीं है, लेकिन यह स्पष्ट नहीं है कि क्या अस्थायी रुकावट "पहुंच की हानि" है और इस प्रकार उल्लंघन है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Constitutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप। इसके Synonyms हैं: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful और Antonyms हैं: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary।

hinglishTracks.en: If yes, a company must report the outage; if not, the company need not report, even if customers complained throughout the day.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — यदि हाँ, तो कंपनी को आउटेज की रिपोर्ट अवश्य करनी चाहिए; यदि नहीं, तो कंपनी को रिपोर्ट करने की आवश्यकता नहीं है, भले ही ग्राहक पूरे दिन शिकायत करते रहें।।

hinglishTracks.en: Europe’s regulators count even a temporary loss of access as a breach to be logged, but only demand a report if people are put at risk.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — यूरोप के नियामक पहुंच के अस्थायी नुकसान को भी लॉग किए जाने वाले उल्लंघन के रूप में मानते हैं, लेकिन केवल तभी रिपोर्ट की मांग करते हैं जब लोगों को जोखिम में डाला जाता है।।

hinglishTracks.en: A faulty update to Falcon Sensor, a security programme sold by CrowdStrike, caused some 8.5 million Windows computers worldwide to crash on July 19, 2024.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — क्राउडस्ट्राइक द्वारा बेचे जाने वाले सुरक्षा कार्यक्रम फाल्कन सेंसर के एक दोषपूर्ण अपडेट के कारण 19 जुलाई, 2024 को दुनिया भर में लगभग 8.5 मिलियन विंडोज कंप्यूटर क्रैश हो गए।।

hinglishTracks.en: The machines showed a blue error screen, known as the “Blue Screen of Death”, and kept crashing until the faulty file was removed.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — मशीनों ने एक नीली त्रुटि स्क्रीन दिखाई, जिसे "ब्लू स्क्रीन ऑफ़ डेथ" के रूप में जाना जाता है, और दोषपूर्ण फ़ाइल हटाए जाने तक क्रैश होती रही।।

hinglishTracks.en: IndiGo cancelled 283 flights.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — इंडिगो ने 283 उड़ानें रद्द कीं.।

hinglishTracks.en: This week, the computers did not crash as the failure was in Microsoft’s own data centres.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — इस सप्ताह, कंप्यूटर क्रैश नहीं हुए क्योंकि विफलता Microsoft के अपने डेटा केंद्रों में थी।।

hinglishTracks.en: Following the incident, CERT-In issued a “critical” advisory and Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw said his Ministry was in touch with Microsoft.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — घटना के बाद, सीईआरटी-इन ने एक "महत्वपूर्ण" सलाह जारी की और केंद्रीय इलेक्ट्रॉनिक्स और सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी मंत्री अश्विनी वैष्णव ने कहा कि उनका मंत्रालय माइक्रोसॉफ्ट के संपर्क में है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The European Union and the U.K.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — यूरोपीय संघ और यू.के.।

hinglishTracks.en: have placed the biggest tech vendors directly under financial regulators’ watch.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — सबसे बड़े तकनीकी विक्रेताओं को सीधे वित्तीय नियामकों की निगरानी में रखा गया है।।

hinglishTracks.en: The EU’s financial supervisors named 19 such companies under its Digital Operational Resilience Act on November 18, 2025, which includes Microsoft and Tata Consultancy Services.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — यूरोपीय संघ के वित्तीय पर्यवेक्षकों ने 18 नवंबर, 2025 को अपने डिजिटल ऑपरेशनल रेजिलिएंस एक्ट के तहत 19 ऐसी कंपनियों को नामित किया, जिनमें माइक्रोसॉफ्ट और टाटा कंसल्टेंसी सर्विसेज शामिल हैं।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Resilience' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: लचीलापन और मज़बूती — किसी बड़े संकट या मंदी के बाद तेज़ी से वापस उभरने की क्षमता। इसके Synonyms हैं: Robustness, Endurance, Adaptability और Antonyms हैं: Fragility, Vulnerability, Weakness।

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (16 NOV)

📰 How does India address service outages?

📌 Published: 16 Nov 2026, 10:56:28 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Does Indian law require Microsoft to have reported the recent outage that affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite? What rules apply in such situations and what are their shortcomings in the present form? How are cloud companies accountable in other countries? What are Indian customers’ options?

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: From November 12 to 13, an as-yet unspecified problem with Microsoft infrastructure affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite Microsoft 365 worldwide, including its Outlook email service. Microsoft apologised during the outage and attributed the incident to a fault in an upgrade of its network capacity, although more precise details are still expected. In India, among consequences in various sectors, IndiGo and Akasa Air alerted passengers of disruptions to their email support while Air India rerouted its email. The incident raises larger questions about whether companies providing services on which lakhs of people depend are required to account for such failures in India. First, the directions issued by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) on April 28, 2022, under the Information Technology Act, 2000, require companies to report cyber incidents within six hours. The directions cover attacks and intrusions but not outages caused by technical faults. Still, CERT-In can call for information under Section 70B(6) of the IT Act to seek an explanation from Microsoft. The second is the Reserve Bank of India’s directions on managing risks in outsourcing, issued on November 28, 2025. They carry forward rules on outsourced IT services that first took effect on October 1, 2023. A bank buying cloud services must assess its dependence on the supplier and have an exit strategy. If the arrangement fails, the RBI can hold the bank responsible and the bank can seek an explanation from Microsoft under its agreement. The third is the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. The Act defines a personal data breach to include an accidental “loss of access to personal data”. Under Rules set to come into effect in May 2027, data breaches must be reported to the Data Protection Board and to each affected person. Failure to report could attract a penalty of up to ₹200 crore. The onus is on the organisation that collected the data, and the organisation is Microsoft’s customer, even though the data sits on Microsoft’s servers. While Indian law does not require a minimum threshold of harm to report a breach, it is unclear whether a temporary outage constitutes a “loss of access” and thus a breach. If yes, a company must report the outage; if not, the company need not report, even if customers complained throughout the day. Europe’s regulators count even a temporary loss of access as a breach to be logged, but only demand a report if people are put at risk. A faulty update to Falcon Sensor, a security programme sold by CrowdStrike, caused some 8.5 million Windows computers worldwide to crash on July 19, 2024. The machines showed a blue error screen, known as the “Blue Screen of Death”, and kept crashing until the faulty file was removed. IndiGo cancelled 283 flights. This week, the computers did not crash as the failure was in Microsoft’s own data centres. Following the incident, CERT-In issued a “critical” advisory and Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw said his Ministry was in touch with Microsoft.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The European Union and the U.K. have placed the biggest tech vendors directly under financial regulators’ watch. The EU’s financial supervisors named 19 such companies under its Digital Operational Resilience Act on November 18, 2025, which includes Microsoft and Tata Consultancy Services. Thus, an Indian company already reports to European supervisors.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility
Resilience (Noun)
लचीलापन और मज़बूती — किसी बड़े संकट या मंदी के बाद तेज़ी से वापस उभरने की क्षमता।
✓ Syn: Robustness, Endurance, Adaptability  |  ✖ Ant: Fragility, Vulnerability, Weakness
Productivity (Noun)
उत्पादकता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Productivity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "How does India address service outages?", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Does Indian law require Microsoft to have reported the recent outage that affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite?.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'How does India address service outages?' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'How does India address service outages?' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'How does India address service outages?' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Does Indian law require Microsoft to have reported the recent outage that affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite?." (Hinglish Arth: क्या भारतीय कानून के अनुसार माइक्रोसॉफ्ट को हालिया आउटेज की रिपोर्ट करने की आवश्यकता है जिससे ग्राहकों की उत्पादकता सूट तक पहुंचने की क्षमता प्रभावित हुई है?)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "How does India address service outages?"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Thus, an Indian company already reports to European supervisors.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Thus, an Indian company already reports to European supervisors." (Hinglish Arth: इस प्रकार, एक भारतीय कंपनी पहले से ही यूरोपीय पर्यवेक्षकों को रिपोर्ट करती है।)

articles.title: Orbital computing could let scientists rent ‘brainpower’ in space

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: To bridge the gap between data being recorded by satellites and data being available to users on the ground, operators are pursuing a solution called in-orbit computing: the basic idea is to analyse some data onboard the satellite and only send back the most relevant information

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Satellites observe floods by capturing images of inundated areas such as submerged roads, damaged infrastructure, and settlements in the path of flood waters. This data helps response teams make critical decisions but only if the data reaches them in time. To be useful in emergencies, data must get to users quickly.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Today’s satellites monitor everything from weather to agriculture to our oceans. As satellite technology improves, so does the quality of the data they provide, giving us more and better information about our planet and its inhabitants. However, there is a gap between data being recorded and data being available to users on the ground. It has to be sent to the earth, downloaded at ground stations during satellite pass windows, then analysed in time for it to be put to use.

📰 Orbital computing could let scientists rent ‘brainpower’ in space

🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: To bridge the gap between data being recorded by satellites and data being available to users on the ground, operators are pursuing a solution called in-orbit computing: the basic idea is to analyse some data onboard the satellite and only send back the most relevant information

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Satellites observe floods by capturing images of inundated areas such as submerged roads, damaged infrastructure, and settlements in the path of flood waters. This data helps response teams make critical decisions but only if the data reaches them in time. To be useful in emergencies, data must get to users quickly.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Today’s satellites monitor everything from weather to agriculture to our oceans. As satellite technology improves, so does the quality of the data they provide, giving us more and better information about our planet and its inhabitants. However, there is a gap between data being recorded and data being available to users on the ground. It has to be sent to the earth, downloaded at ground stations during satellite pass windows, then analysed in time for it to be put to use.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Restoration of Statehood is essential for peace in Jammu and Kashmir

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days. On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured. On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam. In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11. The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths. The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns. Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days. The Omar Abdullah government , because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung. The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined. According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: That said, the decline in terrorist incidents and the silence of the streets should not be mistaken for peace. The current situation demands a political reach-out by the Centre to all the stakeholders of J&K. It has to begin with the much-promised restoration of Statehood , which will give the voters a sense that their mass participation in the 2024 Assembly elections allowed their elected leaders to hold institutions accountable, and they were able to work freely to protect the interests of the region. Though the security agencies need to be focused on Pakistan-backed terrorism, it should not come at the cost of re-inflicting psychological scars within Kashmir, which could turn into a powder keg if left unattended. Healing through both political and security processes has to be complementary rather than conflicting. Allowing the political class of J&K to establish its writ and providing room to security agencies to combat challenges are not contradictory.

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Death penalty requires a near-infallible criminal justice system

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s vote against a proposed global moratorium on the death penalty at the UN is consistent with its position at the forum; it has defended its retention of the penalty as a sovereign decision backed by judicial safeguards, including the “rarest of rare” condition and sessions courts’ sentences requiring a High Court’s confirmation. At the same time, the Supreme Court has increasingly restricted capital punishment and research has failed to find evidence of additional deterrence over life imprisonment . India’s distinction between judicial executions and extrajudicial killings is legally valid but its further claim that due process protects people facing execution is less so. While India last executed convicts in 2020, for the Delhi gang-rape and murder, Parliament expanded the number of capital offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita — a form of penal populism that projects the political attractiveness of the state’s response to public outrage, especially in cases of sexual violence, without addressing the poor policing and low conviction rates that actually undermine deterrence . The country had 574 people on death row on December 31, 2025, the highest since 2016, thanks to trial court rulings, challenging claims about judicial safeguards in practice. The report of the 2015 Law Commission headed by Justice A.P. Shah said the death penalty “fails to achieve any constitutionally valid penological goals” and recommended abolishing it for all crimes except terrorism and waging war. Only a small group of countries worldwide are executing more people. In India, per Project 39A, the Supreme Court released 38 persons from death row in 2016-2025 after they had spent eight years there on average. Some have endured more than two decades. The punishment requires a measure of infallibility that the criminal justice system cannot supply. The safeguards neither deter convictions in cases with flawed evidence, false testimony, and so on nor remedy unequal access to competent legal representation among those facing the penalty. India should formally suspend executions and commission a review of penalty statutes and the treatment of prisoners on death row. Second, it should spare offences that do not involve intentional killing from the penalty. Research suggests meting out excessively harsh punishments for non-fatal crimes could incentivise offenders to escalate their violence, including to kill potential witnesses. The greater goal should be to abolish the practice in law while improving investigative and prosecutorial practices and access to legal aid.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: prison / judiciary (system of justice) / crime, law and justice / United Nations / death penalty policies

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The dangers of centralising the internet’s architecture are now clear

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Last week, Microsoft’s suite of productivity and email software, which businesses, governments, hospitals and a host of other organisations rely upon round-the-clock, abruptly stopped working globally , affecting tens of millions of people around the world. The company has cited a network upgrade gone awry as the root cause of the incident. Incidents such as the Microsoft 365 outage are a natural consequence of businesses and governments allowing key digital systems to become centralised all over the world. The internet remains, and was pioneered as, a network of networks. If one business’s networks went down, the reasoning went, others would not fall like dominos: everyone was, after all, connected to everyone else. But the economics have long been prohibitive, with dedicated servers and web-connected infrastructure infeasible for all but the largest businesses, with even those firms seeking the enticing cost savings from socialised infrastructure. That made sense: the internet made shared infrastructure more economical, allowing hardware and maintenance costs to be spread so far and wide that at a per-user level prices have been negligible. Competition among major cloud providers, the few that remain at Microsoft’s scale, have kept prices affordable for enterprise software for all shades of organisations.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Digital services have grown more sophisticated, and more deeply integrated into the economy as this centralisation unfolded. But the downside is that, regardless of the sophistication and professionalism of any company, mistakes happen, and the scale of these mistakes can quickly cascade over to the entire economy. There are societal and organisational lessons to be gleaned from these episodes. There is no such thing as a reliable vendor. Governments must also draw a cyber sovereignty lesson here that does not simply entail swapping a global vendor for a domestic one. It is the subversion of the internet’s architecture that is at the root of these incidents. Investing in resilience — and shielding critical operations from destabilising disruptions, no matter how improbable — should inform attitudes to digital systems. As a new generation of AI data centres is poised to supercharge the centralised systems of yesteryear, it is all the more imperative to mitigate even occasional vagaries of large systems.

1. Core Context & Background: India should use multilateral fora to advance bilateral cooperation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While maintaining its hard stance on cross-border terrorism, India has an opportunity to recognise that many of its other interests still merit sustained cooperation with Pakistan as the latter’s climate minister Musadik Masood Malik prepares to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi. India’s official position since the Pahalgam attack and the ensuing confrontations along the border is that terrorism and bilateral talks cannot coexist. A month later, Prime Minister Narendra Modi signalled that India’s relations with Pakistan would remain subordinate to its demands on cross-border terrorism by extending the condition to trade and water. South Asia is already one of the least economically integrated regions worldwide, with intra-regional trade at around 5%, and, as Chatham House has inferred, strained ties between India and its neighbours have created diplomatic vacuums that Beijing has taken advantage of through trilateral and regional groupings. Now, by inviting all SCO members to the national capital and participating in meetings ahead of the August 2027 Islamabad Summit, New Delhi has shown some maturity as a convening power. Islamabad is also being pragmatic in keeping channels open during its SCO chairmanship by participating in an initiative championed by Mr. Modi.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The pursuit of regionwide water security remains particularly fluid, with India seemingly overlooking the fact that it is upstream of Pakistan and Bangladesh and downstream of China. After India stopped sharing routine hydrological data of the Indus river and approved the Chenab-Beas link tunnel project, Mr. Malik fanned the flames saying Pakistan would “cut off those hands” seeking to restrict its share of the water. Yet China has now restricted the same data vis-à-vis the Brahmaputra while it builds the Medog mega-dam in Tibet. India has also protested the proposed Padma Barrage in Bangladesh, which has been increasing its alignment with China, echoing India building the Farakka Barrage over East Pakistan’s objections in 1961. Climate change is rendering cooperation more essential to manage the integrity of contested geographies, the willingness of border populations to engage, and the potential to generate hydroelectric power. New Delhi should retreat from the notion that working together on the Indus will be a concession to Islamabad and see in the Dialogue an opportunity to restore the necessary channels. Suspending ties may communicate political resolve but will not diminish terrorists’ capabilities in the region or improve India’s security. It has already compromised India’s ambitions to regional leadership, which require the ability to keep engaging even with difficult neighbours. India should go beyond using multilateral fora to assert its national position and start identifying areas where bilateral cooperation serves its interests, including with Pakistan.

1. Core Context & Background: Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America. Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Israel-US strikes on Iran / Iran / USA / armed conflict / war

dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners. Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.
