dailyQuiz10.explanation:
1. Core Context & Background: Ukraine has targeted the structure several times, latest on November 17, 2026

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: In 2022, Ukraine bombed the Kerch bridge linking mainland Russia to the Crimean Peninsula, using explosives hidden in a truck. In 2023, naval drones struck the bridge. In 2025, covert Ukrainian operatives planted bombs on its undersea support pillars. But none of these attacks caused major damage to the structure, which Russian President Vladimir Putin described in 2018 as a “miracle”. But earlier this week, two back-to-back Ukrainian attacks, involving drones and missiles, brought down a crucial span of the road bridge and damaged the parallel rail bridge. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed it as an “unprecedented operation”. Russian authorities acknowledged the damage, announcing a suspension of road traffic and restrictions on train services. The 19-km Kerch bridge , across the Kerch Strait, which connects the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, is the longest bridge in Europe, built at a cost of $3.6 billion. It was opened in 2018 by Russian President Vladimir Putin, four years after Russia annexed Crimea from Ukraine through a contested referendum. Mr. Putin drove an orange truck across its length and said “a miracle has come true”. The bridge is important for Russia for symbolic, administrative and operational reasons. When Russia swiftly moved to annex Crimea in 2014 , after a pro-Russian elected government in Kyiv fell amid West-backed anti-regime protests, there was no direct connectivity between the Russian mainland and the peninsula, which hosts Russia’s Black Sea fleet. Mr. Putin immediately ordered the construction of the bridge. But the bridge remained a weak link as Ukraine grew in military strength, backed by the West, in subsequent years. This 2017 photo shows the newly installed railroad arch of a road-and-rail bridge under construction to connect the Russian mainland with Crimea, at dawn in the Kerch Strait, Crimea. | Photo Credit: Reuters When Mr. Putin ordered the invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022 (what Russia calls a ‘special military operation’), one of the military objectives, according to experts, was to secure a “land bridge” from southwest Russia to Crimea, where 77% of the local population identified Russian as their native language. Today, Russia has the land bridge extending from northeastern Ukraine through the Donbas and Kherson to Crimea. But the bridge remains a critical logistical supply link for the Russian troops in the south. And for Crimea, which depends on mainland Russia for much of its food, fuel and consumer goods, the bridge is also an economic lifeline. If Russia sees the bridge as a symbol of pride, Ukraine sees it as a symbol of occupation. Russia also used Crimea as a launchpad to start its 2022 invasion. That’s why Ukrainians have repeatedly targeted the bridge. The context of the latest attack is also significant. The attack came just days ahead of President Putin’s trilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. According to Mr. Zelenskyy, Ukraine carried out a seven-stage operation, disabling Russian radars, air defence and electronic warfare systems protecting the bridge, before launching a two-tier attack with missiles and drones. The damage caused to the bridge, according to Ukraine, is a blow to Mr. Putin. Russia built a myth around it as a symbol of Crimea being ‘Russian forever’,” the Ukrainian military said in a statement after the attack.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While the damage caused to the Kerch bridge and the halt in traffic are clearly a setback to Russia, the impact would be less consequential for Moscow than what it would have been in 2022. Before the war, Russia was almost entirely dependent on the bridge to move people, goods and equipment across the Kerch strait. But today, Russia has a land corridor connecting its southeast with the Crimean Peninsula. Russia has also started ferry services across the strait which could offset the impact of any disruption in traffic on the bridge. Yet, the attack shows Ukraine’s growing capability to strike even Russia’s most fortified infrastructure as both sides continue to exchange fire.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Three of Hyderabad’s prominent shopping destinations — Jubilee Hills, Banjara Hills and Himayatnagar — have featured in the Asia-Pacific (APAC) rankings of the world’s leading retail streets, according to the latest report by global real estate consultancy Cushman and Wakefield. The figures offer an indication of the rental costs associated with securing retail space in some of Hyderabad’s established shopping districts. Jubilee Hills secured the 51st position in the regional rankings, with prime retail rents estimated at ₹250 per square feet per month. Banjara Hills and Himayatnagar jointly occupied the 52nd position, with corresponding rents of ₹230 and ₹225 per square feet per month, respectively. For instance, renting a 1,000 square feet outlet in Jubilee Hills would translate into an indicative monthly rental expenditure of ₹2.5 lakh, compared with ₹2.3 lakh in Banjara Hills and ₹2.25 lakh in Himayatnagar. The findings are part of the 36th edition of Cushman and Wakefield’s ‘Main Streets Across the World 2026’ report, which examines headline rents across 147 leading retail locations globally. Hyderabad’s three shopping destinations feature alongside several other Indian retail streets in the APAC rankings, reflecting the representation of multiple Indian cities among the region’s prominent retail markets. Delhi’s Khan Market retained its position as India’s highest-ranked retail street, occupying the 25th position in APAC and 24th globally. Its headline rents increased 14% year-on-year to approximately ₹1,875 per square feet per month. Mumbai’s Linking Road ranked 33rd, with monthly rents of ₹1,175 per sq. ft. It also recorded the highest rental growth across Asia-Pacific at 28% year-on-year. Other Indian retail destinations featured in the rankings included Vittal Mallya Road, Brigade Road and Indiranagar in Bengaluru, JM Road, MG Road and FC Road in Pune, Park Street and Gariahat in Kolkata and Anna Nagar and Pondy Bazaar in Chennai. The report identified India as the strongest-performing market in the Asia-Pacific region, with several high streets recording double-digit rental growth. Prime retail rents across APAC increased 3.1% year-on-year in the 12 months to the third quarter of 2026, compared with 2.3% in the corresponding period a year earlier. “India’s retail market continues to demonstrate strong fundamentals, supported by resilient consumption, sustained retailer expansion and increasing premiumisation,” said Milin Rohinesh, head of Retail-India at Cushman and Wakefield.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At the global level, New York City’s Upper Fifth Avenue reclaimed its position as the world’s most expensive retail street, with rents increasing 35% over the past year to US$2,700 per square feet annually. The street moved from third position in 2025 to first, reclaiming the top spot for the first time since 2023.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has sought immediate financial assistance from the Union government to help the State cope with the damage caused by two successive cyclones (Arnab and Murasu), which inflicted losses estimated at over ₹7,000 crore. During a meeting with Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi on November 17, 2026 (Tuesday), Mr. Naidu explained the impact of the two cyclones on agriculture, power infrastructure and other sectors, and urged her to extend immediate financial support. He said crops nearing harvest had been damaged, leaving farmers in distress. Despite the impact of El Niño, the State had supplied irrigation water to some regions through the Pattiseema project to help the farmers, but the successive cyclones caused extensive crop losses, the Chief Minister said. Coastal infrastructure, particularly the power distribution network, suffered considerable damage. The Chief Minister said Central teams had visited the State to assess the damage and were expected to submit their reports soon. Immediate assistance, even before completion of the assessment process, would provide some financial relief to the State, he said. The Chief Minister also discussed region-wise development plans for Visakhapatnam, Amaravati and Tirupati. Mr. Naidu recalled that Ms. Sitharaman had laid the stone for the Rayalaseema Horticulture Hub, and sought the release of funds for developing supporting infrastructure, including rural roads, irrigation facilities and drip irrigation systems. He also sought additional Central assistance for the Visakhapatnam Economic Region (VER), saying it was witnessing rapid growth and that further support would help extend the benefits of development to the people. The Chief Minister briefed the Finance Minister about the recent CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam, including the investment proposals and discussions held during the two-day event.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: State Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav, MPs and senior Finance Department officials attended the meeting.
